text: design/nodes/mechanical.gearboxes.json (untouched, rev 5) still records gear_ratio 148.3, no_load_speed 0.459 rad/s and torque_peak/reaction_moment 110 kgf*cm (all from R1.07/R1.10/R2.11, the old 50:1 motor), while the revision rewrote mechanical.drivetrain.json gear_ratio to 86.1, control.balance_loop.json torque_peak to 38.7 kgf*cm and control.speed_loop.json no_load_speed to 1.34 rad/s (R1a.05/R1a.02/R2.10, the new 30:1 motor) -- mechanical.gearboxes constrains exactly those three nodes plus firmware.odometry and was never changed, never given a no_change_justified entry, and no owed follow-up was named for it. The design is now internally contradictory about the drivetrain's own gear ratio and torque. Separately, the motor swap also re-cites the 6 V rated-voltage stall current everywhere without scaling to the pack's highest voltage, with no driver-limit comparison, no stall-duration statement, no sourced NiMH discharge-rate check, and all battery-rail checks only at nominal 7.2 V.

electrical.power.json's rewritten motor_current_draw (3.0 A) and motor_power_draw (21.6 W) are never compared against any declared continuous or peak rating of a supply element; no such rating exists in electrical.battery_pack.json, electrical.motor_drivers.json or electrical.control_board.json even though electrical.motor_drivers.json already cites the DRV8838 datasheet (as the source of its thermal_resistance), where continuous/peak current ratings are published and could have been transcribed and compared. This is the revision's duty once it rewrote a load on that rail.

No node in the design graph declares a continuous or peak current rating for any series element (driver, connector, trace, fuse) in the motor-current path, so the rail limit is never shown to be the lowest rating in its path; same gap as [rule], re-triggered by the rewritten motor_current_draw.

electrical.power.json's motor_current_draw (a load drawn from the battery) was rewritten (source changed from [R1.03] to [R1a.04]) to 3.0 A, but electrical.battery_pack.json (untouched) names no cell discharge-rate/C-rate limit anywhere, and the revision neither sourced one for the Pololu AA NiMH cell (#1003) nor showed the 3.0 A draw within a published discharge curve.

electrical.power.json, electrical.motor_drivers.json and electrical.battery_pack.json all state supply_voltage as a single nominal 7.2 V; no check anywhere uses the top of the window or the sagged bottom under the 3.0 A motor load, even though the revision rewrote a battery-rail load.

electrical.motors.json records stall_current/current_draw as 1.5 A at the motor's rated voltage of 6 V (R1a.04), and electrical.power.json's motor_current_draw (3.0 A = 1.5 A x 2) uses that same rated-voltage figure directly; no node anywhere computes I_stall,max = V_max/R scaled to the pack's highest voltage (about 8.4 V fully charged, or even the 7.2 V nominal supply_voltage already recorded in the same nodes).

No node compares the motor's (unscaled or scaled) stall current against the DRV8838's continuous rating, peak rating or minimum OCP trip; electrical.motor_drivers.json records only max_input_voltage, supply_voltage and thermal_resistance, no current ratings at all, for either the old or the new motor.

No node states how long a stall may last or what ends it for the new motor, nor compares an expected continuous current against the maker's 25%-of-stall guidance; absent for both the prior and the new motor.

The motor is a part in the power path and was changed by this revision, but no node records operating/rated ratios for its voltage, current, power or temperature (a derating table per skill 'the derating record'); this record is absent for both the old and the new motor.

electrical.motors.json's constrains list names mechanical.gearboxes directly, and electrical.motors' gear_ratio (29.86 vs 51.45), no_load_speed (115 vs 68.1 rad/s) and stall_torque (0.45 vs 0.74 kgf*cm) are physically changed. design/nodes/mechanical.gearboxes.json (rev 5, untouched) still carries gear_ratio 148.3, no_load_speed 0.459 rad/s and torque_peak/reaction_moment 110 kgf*cm, all derived from the old motor's rows (R1.07, R1.10, R2.11). No change in this change set, no no_change_justified entry, and no named owed follow-up exists for mechanical.gearboxes, so [rule] fails; the design graph now holds two contradictory values (86.1 vs 148.3; 38.7 vs 110 kgf*cm) for what mechanical.gearboxes itself declares it constrains (mechanical.drivetrain, control.balance_loop, control.speed_loop, firmware.odometry) alongside the correctly-updated sibling nodes.
All touched nodes on the battery rail use only the single nominal 7.2 V figure; no top-of-window or sagged-bottom voltage appears anywhere for the rewritten motor-current load.

electrical.motors.json/electrical.power.json use the 1.5 A stall current taken at the motor's rated 6 V directly as the budget/driver-facing figure, with no scaling to the pack's higher voltage (7.2 V nominal, ~8.4 V at full charge).

electrical.motors.json's rewritten stall_current (1.5 A @ 6 V) and electrical.motor_drivers.json's unchanged driver ratings (per standards.md Sec.5, the same DRV8838 is rated 1.8 A peak / 1.9 A minimum trip) are never checked together. Scaling the written stall current to the pack's highest voltage per the skill procedure (I_stall,max = V_max/R, R = 6V/1.5A = 4 ohm; at ~8.4 V, I_stall,max ~= 2.1 A) exceeds both the driver's peak rating and its trip level, by reading, yet no comparison of the motor and driver together exists anywhere in the design graph for either motor.

mechanical.chassis.json's no_change_justified for electrical.motors states the 30:1 motor 'has the same 10 x 12 x 25 mm body' as the 50:1, but parts_sheet.json gives no dimension for either motor (R1.22 and R1a.08 are both null) and no other source for this figure appears anywhere in the design graph; this numeric claim, used to help justify skipping a chassis update, has no producing source even though the node's mass-based justification (9.5 g, sourced to R1a.07) independently supports the same conclusion.

Two confirmable inconsistencies in the revision's own written values: (1) design/nodes/mechanical.drivetrain.json 'supported_mass' was changed from 'derived: [R11.01] - [R10.03] + [R5.07] * [R5.10]' = 330 g (journal rev 4) to 'derived: [R11.01] - [R10.03]' = 165 g (journal rev 36), dropping the battery-mass term with no no_change_justified entry and no stated reason; this is unrelated to the motor's gear ratio and leaves mechanical.drivetrain.supported_mass (165 g) inconsistent with the unwritten mechanical.wheel_left/mechanical.wheel_right nodes, whose 'supported_mass' is still '([R11.01]-[R10.03]+[R5.07]*[R5.10])/[R9.06]' = 165 g each (330 g combined), and with mechanical.robot.mass (still 330 g, unchanged). (2) control.speed_loop and firmware.odometry both record counts_per_wheel_revolution = 2620 with the cited source 'derived: [R3.02] * [R2.12]', but [R3.02] (12) x [R2.12] (218.5) = 2622, not 2620 (parts_sheet.json rows R3.02, R2.12); the recorded number does not match its own cited formula. Together these show the revision was not made fully consistent with the design it changes.

electrical.motor_drivers, electrical.power and firmware.motor_output all still check the new motor/driver load only at the pack's nominal 7.2 V (supply_voltage fields), never at the window's top (~8.4 V open-circuit for 6x NiMH) or the sagged bottom; this is unchanged from before the motor swap and the revision, having re-derived the motor's load figures, did not add the top/bottom check.

electrical.motors.stall_current for the new #3074 motor is recorded as 1.5 A at its rated 6 V (journal rev 30, same as the old #3073 figure), and no node anywhere in the design graph derives I_stall,max at the pack's highest voltage (~8.4 V) for the new motor; per skill 'checking a motor against its driver' step 1 this bound (R = V_rated/I_stall = 4 ohm, I_stall,max = V_max/R) is the revision's own duty whenever the motor is changed, and it was not produced.

No comparison of the new motor's stall current (at any voltage) against electrical.motor_drivers' continuous rating, peak rating or minimum OCP trip appears anywhere in the design graph, and electrical.motor_drivers itself records no such current ratings (only max_input_voltage, supply_voltage, thermal_resistance), so none of the three required comparisons is shown.

No quantity or record in the design graph states how long the new motor may stall or what ends the stall (driver trip or firmware limit); this is unaddressed both before and after the motor swap, and the swap is the trigger that puts it on this revision.

No stress-ratio record (operating/rated ratio for voltage, current, power or temperature, with condition and source) exists for the new #3074 motor anywhere in the design graph, although the motor is a power-path part the revision just chose.

(1) control.speed_loop and firmware.odometry record counts_per_wheel_revolution = 2620 with cited source 'derived: [R3.02] * [R2.12]'; redoing the arithmetic, [R3.02]=12 (parts_sheet.json) x [R2.12]=218.5 = 2622, not 2620: the cited source does not give the recorded number. (2) electrical.motors.no_load_speed is recorded as 45.0 rad/s sourced directly to https://www.pololu.com/product/3074/specs, but that same URL (parts_sheet.json R1a.10) states 430 rpm, not 45.0 rad/s; the rad/s figure is an uncredited unit conversion (430 rpm x 2*pi/60 = 45.03 rad/s), not a value the cited source itself states, repeating the same mislabeling already present for the old motor's 68.1 rad/s figure.

electrical.motor_drivers, electrical.power and firmware.motor_output continue to use only the pack's nominal 7.2 V after the motor swap; the window's top (~8.4 V) and sagged bottom are never used to re-check the new motor's load, matching this antipattern.

The revision leaves the design graph inconsistent: mechanical.gearboxes (rev 30) and control.speed_loop (rev 35) were updated to the new 47:19/127.3 ratio, but firmware.odometry (rev 26, untouched) still holds counts_per_wheel_revolution=1780 derived from the old ratio [R2.11]=148.3, with no follow-up change or no_change_justified entry for that edge of mechanical.gearboxes.constrains. Two of the revision's own no_change_justified notes (firmware.speed_task, firmware.main) incorrectly assert that firmware.odometry already carries 'the new counts per wheel revolution' / 'a new counts-per-wheel-revolution constant', which is false on the record.

control.speed_loop.counts_per_wheel_revolution (written, now 1530) and firmware.odometry.counts_per_wheel_revolution (given, still 1780) represent the same physical wheel-encoder constant after the same gear-ratio change but now disagree by ~16%; judged against its neighbour, firmware.odometry's magnitude is stale and wrong under the new ratio.

mechanical.gearboxes.constrains=[mechanical.drivetrain, control.balance_loop, control.speed_loop, firmware.odometry] (design/nodes/mechanical.gearboxes.json). The first three got a follow-up change or no_change_justified; firmware.odometry (design/nodes/firmware.odometry.json, unchanged since journal rev 26) got neither, despite holding a quantity (counts_per_wheel_revolution) directly derived from the changed gear ratio.

The revision sizes a gear ratio (external_gear_ratio and gear_ratio both changed) but records no usable-torque-vs-wheel-torque check, no motor-current margin, no traction check against μ_s, no floor surface, and no stated governing limit or margin anywhere in the touched nodes or the rest of the design graph; mechanical.gearboxes.torque_peak is the stall-based limit-load reaction (appropriate as a load case per std §1) but is not presented as, nor substitutes for, the required operating torque/traction margin statement. Since the check involves a value the revision wrote (gear_ratio), the missing μ_s/floor/margin is the revision's own duty, not a missing input.

design/journal.jsonl rev 30 (mechanical.gearboxes): the revision's new reaction_moment formula 'derived: [R1.07] * [R2.17] / [R2.26]' = 40.8 kgf*cm no longer balances the same node's torque_peak (81.5 kgf*cm) it is declared to react, whereas the pre-revision node (rev 5) had reaction_moment identically equal to torque_peak (both 110). This is an unjustified, newly introduced inconsistency (see [rule]/[rule]). The revision also resizes the gear ratio (rev 30-31) without recording any traction/mu_s/margin check anywhere it touched ([rule]), and its no_load_speed formulas (rev 30, rev 35) do not literally recompute to their stated values without an unstated unit-conversion step ([rule]/[rule]). The revision is therefore not fully consistent with the design it changes.

design/journal.jsonl rev 30 and rev 35: no_load_speed's source 'derived: [R1.10] / [R2.17]' literally evaluates to 650/110.2 = 5.90, not the recorded 0.618 rad/s; the source as written does not hold the recorded value without an unstated rpm-to-rad/s conversion.

design/journal.jsonl rev 30 (mechanical.gearboxes.no_load_speed) and rev 35 (control.speed_loop.no_load_speed): dividing R1.10 (650 rpm) by R2.17 (110.2, dimensionless) and labelling the result rad/s silently applies an unstated 2*pi/60 factor; recomputing the stated formula literally does not give the declared unit/value.

design/journal.jsonl rev 30: mechanical.gearboxes.reaction_moment (40.8 kgf*cm) is exactly half of the same node's torque_peak (81.5 kgf*cm), its direct physical neighbour (the torque it is meant to react), with no explanation for the mismatch; pre-revision (rev 5) the two were equal (110 and 110).

design/journal.jsonl rev 30: mechanical.gearboxes declares reaction_moment = 40.8 kgf*cm against the load it reacts, torque_peak = 81.5 kgf*cm, from the same gearbox/wheel; a single mount reacting a single applied torque must show equal and opposite moments for equilibrium, so a reaction of half the applied torque with no second reaction declared and no stated reason is an imbalance.

design/journal.jsonl rev 30-31: the revision resizes mechanical.gearboxes.gear_ratio (148.3 to 110.2) and external_gear_ratio (2.88 to 2.14), explicitly triggering [rule], but no node in the design graph (before or after the revision) records a traction check, a sourced mu_s, a motor-current-vs-25%-stall check, or a stated margin with its governing limit; this duty falls on the revision because it rewrote the very gear-ratio quantities the check depends on.

The revision is not fully consistent with the design it changes: mechanical.gearboxes (journal.jsonl rev 30) changed torque_peak/reaction_moment from 110 to 71.2 kgf*cm and lists control.balance_loop in its 'constrains' edges, but design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json was never touched (absent from both diff parts) and still carries torque_peak = 110 kgf*cm sourced to the discarded ratio 'derived: [R1.07] * [R2.11]'. No no_change_justified was recorded on mechanical.gearboxes for that edge either.

mechanical.gearboxes (journal.jsonl rev 30) constrains control.balance_loop and changed torque_peak/reaction_moment (110 -> 71.2 kgf*cm) and gear_ratio (148.3 -> 96.2). control.balance_loop.json was not written in this revision (absent from diff-01 and diff-02) and still holds torque_peak = 110 kgf*cm, source 'derived: [R1.07] * [R2.11]', i.e. the discarded ratio. No no_change_justified naming control.balance_loop was added to mechanical.gearboxes. The no_change_justified that was written sits on firmware.balance_task and addresses a different edge (control.balance_loop -> firmware.balance_task), not this one. Per the Verdict policy (clause B, Given values): 'A missed follow-up, where a written value is inconsistent with an unwritten one, is a finding against the revision.'

The revision re-sizes the drivetrain's gear ratio (mechanical.gearboxes.json: gear_ratio 148.3 -> 96.2, a ~35% drop in available wheel torque), which triggers [rule], but no node anywhere in the design graph states which limit (motor torque vs. traction) now governs or gives a margin and reason for the new ratio; this was already absent from the pre-revision design and the revision did not add it despite rewriting the governing quantity. The traction sub-check (tractive force <= mu_s*N) additionally cannot be decided at all: no floor surface or mu_s value exists anywhere in the design graph (parts_sheet.json and all design/nodes/*.json), so that specific sub-check is blocked (see blocking defect); the 'margin and governing limit' sub-check is judged independently and fails.

mechanical.drivetrain.supported_mass was changed from 330 g to 370 g (design/nodes/mechanical.drivetrain.json) by adding '[R9.03] * [R9.06]' (wheel-pair mass) on top of a formula whose base terms already include wheel mass per R11.01 (200 g, 'assembled with motors, 80 mm wheels and bumper cage'), double-counting ~40 g against mechanical.robot.mass (still 330 g); and mechanical.robot's no_change_justified reason for this change ('no part is added or removed, so the robot's mass ... unchanged') is contradicted by that very 40 g change in the same commit. Separately, mechanical.gearboxes.torque_peak/control.balance_loop.torque_peak are recomputed in this revision as stall torque (R1.07) x the new gear ratio (R2.23) = 62.5 kgf*cm, treating stall torque as the drive's operating torque, contrary to std §12/skill file. Both are the revision's own written values, making the revision internally inconsistent with the design it changes.

mechanical.drivetrain.supported_mass (370 g) now exceeds mechanical.robot.mass (330 g) by exactly the wheel-pair mass (R9.03 x R9.06 = 0.7 oz x 2 = 39.69 g), even though R11.01 (200 g), the figure both quantities are built from, already includes '80 mm wheels' per its own cited source family (skill file worked example for the same product/3575 URL); the new formula therefore double-counts wheel mass against its neighbour quantity.

mechanical.drivetrain (rev 31) changed supported_mass from 330 g to 370 g in this change set; mechanical.drivetrain constrains mechanical.robot, which the revision also wrote (rev 32) with no_change_justified{'mechanical.drivetrain': 'The gear pair is swapped inside the same gearbox housing; no part is added or removed, so the robot's mass and height are unchanged.'}. That reason addresses only the gear-ratio swap and is contradicted by the numbers: the drivetrain's own mass figure changed by 40 g in the same commit with no part stated as added or removed to explain it.

mechanical.drivetrain.supported_mass, a mass quantity the revision wrote, is derived from a formula that double-counts the wheel-pair mass already included in its own cited parts-sheet row R11.01 (see [rule]), so this mass figure does not correctly follow from the stated parts list and method.

mechanical.gearboxes.torque_peak/reaction_moment and control.balance_loop.torque_peak are computed in this revision as 'derived: [R1.07] * [R2.23]' = 0.74 kgf*cm (R1.07, 'stall torque @ 6V') x 84.4 = 62.5 kgf*cm, using stall torque directly as the drive's operating/design torque for the newly selected ratio, contrary to 'stall torque is not used as an operating point' (std §12, skill file); no statement of which limit (motor or traction) governs the new ratio, nor any margin, accompanies the change.

Same citation as [rule]: mechanical.gearboxes.torque_peak/reaction_moment and control.balance_loop.torque_peak are computed as stall torque (R1.07) times the new overall gear ratio (R2.23=84.4), taking the motor's stall torque as the available/operating torque for the gear-ratio resizing this revision performs.

design/nodes/mechanical.wheel_left.json and design/nodes/mechanical.wheel_right.json: supported_mass was rewritten as 'derived: [R11.01] + [R5.07] * [R5.10]' = 365 g, dropping the prior '/ [R9.06]' per-wheel division (journal.jsonl rev 6/7 show the earlier formula '([R11.01] - [R10.03] + [R5.07] * [R5.10]) / [R9.06]' = 165 g). The new per-wheel value equals the whole-robot total (also 365 g in mechanical.drivetrain.json and mechanical.robot.json), so the two wheels together declare 730 g of support for a 365 g robot — an internal inconsistency the revision itself introduced while writing these nodes.

design/nodes/mechanical.wheel_left.json and mechanical.wheel_right.json: supported_mass=365 g each is identical to the neighbouring mechanical.drivetrain.json supported_mass=365 g (the combined/total figure) and to mechanical.robot.json mass=365 g, instead of each wheel carrying roughly half; comparing the written value against its neighbours shows an inconsistency the prior revision (division by R9.06=2) avoided.

The robot rests on two wheel supports. design/nodes/mechanical.wheel_left.json and mechanical.wheel_right.json declare supported_mass=365 g each (rev 33, rev 34 in design/journal.jsonl); summing the two declared reactions gives 730 g against a 365 g total load (mechanical.robot.json mass=365 g) -- an unbalanced declared reaction, a derived-bound (category 1) violation on values the revision itself wrote.

mechanical.bumper_cage.json is a newly added part (first appearance in design/nodes/mechanical.bumper_cage.json, rev 30) attached to mechanical.robot, but no clearance value (to the wheels, chassis or ground in the balancing pose) is stated anywhere for it; determining this clearance is the revision's own duty as the one introducing the part, so its absence is a finding, not a blocking defect.

design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json (rev 30): loop_gain raised 2.5->3.0, explicitly sourced as the gain that firmware.balance_task's own loop_gain tracks ('design: gain of control.balance_loop', firmware.balance_task.json rev 23). firmware.balance_task.loop_gain was never rewritten and still reads 2.5, directly contradicting the new 3.0 value. The one follow-up the revision made, design/nodes/firmware.main.json (rev 31) adding no_change_justified:{'firmware.balance_task':'...'}, is attached to firmware.main, a node whose own 'constrains' list is empty and which is not named in control.balance_loop's constrains edge; it also only discusses the scheduler tick/clock, not the stale loop_gain. The revision is therefore inconsistent with the design graph it changed.

No node anywhere in design/nodes/*.json states a tilt-angle, speed or load validity range for the linearised/linear plant model behind control.balance_loop's gain; this is tied to the loop_gain value the revision wrote and was never stated, before or after the revision.

No node or journal entry shows closed-loop pole computation for the loop at loop_gain=3.0 (or 2.5); no eigenvalues appear anywhere in the design graph. Chargeable to the revision since it changed the gain whose poles this would check.
No Nyquist encirclement count or pole computation is recorded anywhere in the design graph for either gain value.
No S/PS/CS/T stability computation or closed-loop pole set is recorded anywhere; no reading check against the PID-root condition is shown (and [rule] shows this is not even a PID loop).

The stating line (omega_gc, n_gc, tau_total, tau_common, common RHP zero) is owed regardless of [B] and is nowhere stated in control.balance_loop.json or any other node; this is the revision's duty since it changed the gain that sets omega_gc.

The RHP-zero stating line (owed regardless of [B]; 'none found' must still be stated) is absent from every node; no list of fed-back transfer-function zeros, or a 'none found' statement, appears anywhere in the design graph.

No bandwidth value (motor+driver, IMU+filter) is recorded anywhere in electrical.motors.json, electrical.motor_drivers.json or electrical.imu.json, and no comparison to omega_gc is made; this stating line is owed regardless of [B] and is the revision's duty since it concerns the delivered loop containing the new gain.
No gain or phase margin number appears anywhere in the design graph for either loop_gain value.

No design case (LQR/PID/other) is stated for control.balance_loop and no margin floor is checked; loop_gain's description ('proportional gain') suggests a simple P design, but nothing states this as the case or reports margins against the cat.3 floors.

control.tilt_estimator ('gyro and accelerometer fusion', constrains firmware.imu_driver, feeds control.balance_loop) is an estimator/filter in the balance loop, so this item's trigger is present; since no margin of any kind is computed anywhere ([rule]), none is computed on the correct estimator-inclusive loop either.
No lower gain margin (GML) or stability margin s_m is reported anywhere in the design graph.
No sensitivity peak M_s or complementary sensitivity peak M_T is reported anywhere in the design graph.

No gain margin of any form (ratio or dB) is reported anywhere, so its units cannot be confirmed explicit; this absence is the same missing-margins failure as [rule]/[rule], chargeable to the revision.

No crossover frequency omega_c is computed for the new loop_gain=3.0, so the h*omega_c (or omega*h) ratio required by this item is never argued; sample_rate (100 Hz, control.balance_loop.json) is unchanged but its ratio to the new (unknown) crossover is never re-examined, even though raising the gain changes the crossover.
No margin or crossover computation of any kind exists, continuous or discrete, so the hold/filter phase-cost accounting this item requires cannot be, and was not, shown.

tau_total and tau_common (owed regardless of [B]) are nowhere stated in the design graph; the cat.1 tau_unmodelled < PM/omega_gc check (also owed regardless of [B]) cannot be evaluated since neither PM nor omega_gc is ever computed. Chargeable to the revision since it changed the loop_gain this item concerns.

The cat.2 stating line (A/D resolution and coefficient word length assumed) is owed for the coefficient (loop_gain) the revision wrote and is nowhere stated in control.balance_loop.json or any other node; no simulation or estimate of quantisation effect is shown either.

Trigger present (control.tilt_estimator functions as an observer feeding the balance loop). No run anywhere in the design graph drives the actuator into its declared 6V/0.833-duty limit to confirm the controller state does not keep growing while saturated for the new gain=3.0; this run is the revision's duty since it validates the changed loop. (The separate sub-check confirming the observer is fed the saturated input cannot be checked at all - no firmware code exists anywhere - and is recorded as a non-blocking spec defect.)

No simulation of any kind (step, disturbance, or saturating case) exists anywhere in the design graph for either loop_gain value; this is the revision's duty since it is the only way to validate the new, stiffer gain.
No run from the edge of the (unstated, [rule]) tilt range with actuator limits active is shown recovering; no runs of any kind exist in the design graph.

No simulation exists at all, so there is nothing to confirm uses the same gain (3.0), sample period, estimator, filters and saturation limits as 'the delivered code' (which also does not exist in this worktree).

control.balance_loop.json declares constrains:[firmware.balance_task] and changed loop_gain (2.5->3.0, rev 30). firmware.balance_task.json (rev 23) was never rewritten and still carries loop_gain=2.5, sourced as tracking control.balance_loop's gain exactly. No no_change_justified reason was recorded on control.balance_loop or on firmware.balance_task; instead one was added to firmware.main (rev 31), a node not named in control.balance_loop's constrains list at all, addressing only the scheduler tick/clock, not the stale loop_gain. The constrained module's real follow-up duty is unaddressed.

No simulation run exists anywhere in the design graph, at the nominal point or at any [rule]-range edge, for either loop_gain value; the override (margins/poles at edge equilibria) also fails since nothing is computed at all.

No control simulation of any kind exists, so by construction it lacks the declared actuator limit (firmware.motor_output.json: motor_voltage_limit 6V, max_duty_cycle 0.833); the saturation-free assumption is not ruled out for the new, stiffer gain.

sample_rate remains 100 Hz (control.balance_loop.json, control.req_sample_rate.json) with no stated ratio to the achieved closed-loop bandwidth, before or after raising loop_gain to 3.0; since the new gain plausibly raises the crossover frequency, re-arguing this ratio is the revision's duty and was not done.

No composed run of any kind (controller + estimator + saturation + plant together) exists anywhere in the design graph for the new loop_gain=3.0 (see [rule], [rule], [rule], [rule]); the missing run is the [rule] run.

The no_change_justified entry added to firmware.main.json (rev 31), keyed 'firmware.balance_task', is presented as the propagation follow-up for control.balance_loop's change, but firmware.main is not named in control.balance_loop's constrains list and the entry never addresses firmware.balance_task's own stale loop_gain (still 2.5 vs the new 3.0); this gives the appearance of a satisfied [rule] propagation duty that was not actually satisfied.

design/nodes/firmware.speed_task.json (rev 31): loop_gain is recorded as {value: 0.15, unit: "percent"}, sourced as "design: gain of control.speed_loop". design/nodes/control.speed_loop.json (rev 30) states loop_gain = {value: 0.15, unit: "dimensionless"}. The two nodes claim to carry the same gain but disagree by two orders of magnitude once units are taken literally. Before the revision both nodes agreed at 0.2 dimensionless (journal rev 21/24); the revision broke that consistency while updating the value. This is a value the revision itself wrote, not a given value, so it is judged as a finding against the revision.

design/nodes/firmware.main.json (and journal.jsonl rev 35) changes clock_frequency from 16 MHz to 160 MHz while citing the same source URL (https://www.pololu.com/docs/0J70/all) that design/nodes/electrical.mcu.json (rev 13, unmodified by this revision) cites for a value of 16 MHz for the same physical MCU. The revision offers no new source and no stated rationale tied to the revision's own purpose (raising the balance-loop sample rate, which does not require a 10x clock increase). This is a direct, uncorrected contradiction within the design graph the revision itself produced, making it inconsistent with the design it changes.

The stating line (owed regardless of [B]) requires the work to state ω_gc, the crossover slope n_gc, τ_total, τ_common and any common RHP zero for 'the delivered loop' whose sample_rate this revision wrote (control.balance_loop / firmware.balance_task, 100->200 Hz, design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json, firmware.balance_task.json). None of these values appear anywhere in the design graph for this loop, old or new revision. The interface between mechanical.gearboxes (whose torque_peak the revision changed to 71.2 kgf*cm) and control.balance_loop (whose duplicate torque_peak field was left at the old 110 kgf*cm, sourced to the superseded ratio R2.11) was never reconciled; the misdirected no_change_justified entry on firmware.balance_task shows the gearbox change was evaluated node-by-node rather than checked against the directly coupled control.balance_loop record, and this is visible from the design graph alone (mechanical.gearboxes.json, control.balance_loop.json and firmware.balance_task.json), not only from a trajectory. The finding names the interface that was never checked: mechanical.gearboxes <-> control.balance_loop's torque_peak.

design/nodes/mechanical.drivetrain.json (rev 31) changes 'supported_mass' from 330 g ('derived: [R11.01] - [R10.03] + [R5.07]*[R5.10]') to 370 g by adding '+ [R9.03]*[R9.06]' (wheel mass, 0.7 oz x 2). The skill file's worked example states R11.01 (200 g, product 3575) is already 'assembled with motors, 80 mm wheels and bumper cage', so the wheels' mass is already inside R11.01; the added term double-counts roughly 40 g. This contradicts mechanical.robot's own no_change_justified for mechanical.drivetrain ('no part is added or removed, so the robot's mass and height are unchanged') and is inconsistent with the unchanged given values in mechanical.wheel_left/right (165 g each, summing to 330 g) and mechanical.robot.mass (still 330 g). The revision is therefore not internally consistent with the design it changes.

mechanical.drivetrain.json 'supported_mass' jumps from 330 g to 370 g by adding wheel mass ([R9.03]*[R9.06]) on top of a formula that already equalled the robot's total mass (R11.01 - R10.03 + R5.07*R5.10 = 330 g, matching mechanical.robot.mass=330 g, and matching the sum of mechanical.wheel_left.supported_mass + mechanical.wheel_right.supported_mass = 165+165 = 330 g). R11.01 (200 g) is documented (skill.md, worked example) as already including the 80 mm wheels. The new 370 g figure is therefore an unsupported ~40 g inflation versus its own neighbouring, unchanged quantities, with no explanation for the discrepancy.

mechanical.gearboxes' changed gear_ratio/no_load_speed/torque_peak correctly reached its constrains edges (mechanical.drivetrain rev 31, control.balance_loop rev 33, control.speed_loop rev 35, firmware.odometry rev 37 were all written). mechanical.drivetrain's changed gear_ratio and supported_mass reached mechanical.robot (rev 32), but the no_change_justified reason given there ('The gear pair is swapped inside the same gearbox housing; no part is added or removed, so the robot's mass and height are unchanged') is contradicted by the numbers: mechanical.drivetrain.supported_mass rose by 40 g in the same change set, which only holds if a part's mass was newly counted. Per the rubric, 'a reason that is ... contradicted by the numbers is a finding.'

The revision resizes the drivetrain's gear ratio (mechanical.gearboxes, mechanical.drivetrain) but control.balance_loop.torque_peak is written as 'derived: [R1.07] * [R2.23]' = stall torque (R1.07, 'stall torque @ 6V') times the new ratio, with no derating and no stated operating margin -- the forbidden 'stall torque as an operating point' pattern (std §12). No node written by the revision states which limit (motor or traction) governs, a traction check against mu_s*N, or a stated margin, as [rule] requires for a gear-ratio sizing change.

control.balance_loop.torque_peak (62.5 kgf*cm) is computed as 'derived: [R1.07] * [R2.23]' where R1.07 is the gearmotor's stall torque @ 6 V, applied directly as the design's 'torque_peak' with no derating -- a torque budget figure built from stall torque presented as an available/operating figure, matching the antipattern exactly (std §12).

mechanical.wheel_left.supported_mass and mechanical.wheel_right.supported_mass (design/nodes/mechanical.wheel_left.json, mechanical.wheel_right.json; journal.jsonl rev 33-34) were each written as 365 g ('derived: [R11.01] + [R5.07] * [R5.10]'), dropping the '/ [R9.06]' (number-of-wheels) division the prior revision used (165 g = 330/2). This makes each wheel's supported_mass equal to mechanical.drivetrain.supported_mass (365 g, the whole-robot total, journal.jsonl rev 32) instead of its own half-share, so the two wheels now sum to 730 g against a declared total of 365 g -- an internal inconsistency between values the revision itself wrote in the same changeset. The revision is therefore not consistent with the design it changes.

mechanical.wheel_left.supported_mass and mechanical.wheel_right.supported_mass are each written as 365 g, identical to mechanical.drivetrain.supported_mass (365 g, the whole robot's total mass per design/nodes/mechanical.drivetrain.json), rather than half that (182.5 g) as the superseded formula's '/ [R9.06]' (2 wheels) division produced (165 g = 330/2 previously). Judged against its neighbours (the drivetrain total it must share, and the prior methodology for the same quantity), each wheel's supported_mass is wrong by a factor of 2.

control.balance_loop.loop_gain changed (2.5 to 3.0, design/journal.jsonl rev 30) and control.balance_loop.constrains names firmware.balance_task. firmware.balance_task.json (last written at rev 23) still holds loop_gain=2.5, sourced as 'design: gain of control.balance_loop' - unchanged and now contradicting the upstream value. design/nodes/firmware.speed_task.json (and journal.jsonl rev 31) records loop_gain = 0.15 with unit 'percent' and source 'design: gain of control.speed_loop', while design/nodes/control.speed_loop.json (journal rev 30) records the quantity it is sourced from as loop_gain = 0.15 with unit 'dimensionless'. firmware.speed_task.loop_gain was changed to unit 'percent' with value 0.15 while sourced as 'design: gain of control.speed_loop', whose matching quantity control.speed_loop.loop_gain is 0.15 'dimensionless'; these are different unit-kinds for the same quantity, mirroring exactly the Hz-vs-rad/s, degrees-vs-radians confusion [rule] targets, and no other quantity in the design graph (e.g. firmware.motor_output.max_duty_cycle=0.833, recorded 'dimensionless') uses 'percent' for a ratio, confirming this is an inconsistency introduced by the revision, not an established convention.

design/nodes/firmware.main.json records clock_frequency = 160 MHz citing https://www.pololu.com/docs/0J70/all, but the same cited source, for the same quantity, is recorded in design/nodes/electrical.mcu.json as 16 MHz. control.speed_loop's new sample_rate (journal.jsonl rev 30; design/nodes/control.speed_loop.json) is sourced as 'design: outer wheel speed loop at the tilt loop rate' — a round number (100 Hz) justified purely by matching another loop's execution rate, with no stated ratio (h·ω_c or any bandwidth argument) to the speed loop's own delivered closed-loop frequency. design/nodes/mechanical.gearboxes.json: the revision updated torque_peak's source from 'derived: [R1.07] * [R2.11]' (value 110) to 'derived: [R1.07] * [R5.03] / [R1.02] * [R2.11]' (value 132), reflecting the new 7.2 V operating voltage, but left reaction_moment at the unchanged, pre-revision formula 'derived: [R1.07] * [R2.11]' (value 110, byte-for-byte identical to design/journal.jsonl rev 5, i.e. given, not written). design/nodes/control.speed_loop.json's no_load_speed: {value: 4.38, unit: 'rad/s', source: 'derived: [R1.10] / [R2.11]'}. parts_sheet.json: R1.10 = 650 rpm, R2.11 = 148.3 (dimensionless). 650/148.3 = 4.38, which is the result in rpm (the unit of the one non-dimensionless operand), not rad/s; converting to rad/s requires multiplying by 2*pi/60, giving 0.459 rad/s, exactly the value the design held before this revision (journal.jsonl rev 21: no_load_speed 0.459 rad/s, same source string, sample_rate 50 Hz). The revision's new value keeps the 'rad/s' unit label but drops the conversion factor, an unsupported/wrong conversion arithmetic, which [rule] treats as a derived bound (category 1).

design/nodes/control.req_sample_rate.json (and journal.jsonl rev 30) write sample_rate = 5 Hz as the new minimum. design/nodes/control.tilt_estimator.json and design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json (journal.jsonl rev 31, rev 32), written in the same changeset, both add no_change_justified text reading '100 Hz is above the relaxed 50 Hz minimum' — citing a 50 Hz minimum that does not exist anywhere in the design graph; the actual written minimum is 5 Hz. control.req_sample_rate constrains control.tilt_estimator and control.balance_loop (design/nodes/control.req_sample_rate.json 'constrains' list); both received a no_change_justified follow-up (journal.jsonl rev 31, rev 32). A follow-up reason that does not correctly describe the change it is meant to justify does not establish why the change has no effect on the constrained node; this is not merely generic, it is factually wrong about the quantity it cites.

control.req_sample_rate.quantities.sample_rate was changed to the round number 5 Hz (journal.jsonl rev 30) with source text unchanged from a generic 'design: minimum update rate...' description and no stated ratio to any crossover frequency, natural frequency, or derivation of any kind; the only accompanying text (the no_change_justified entries) does not derive the number either, and in fact cites a different number (50 Hz) than the one written, showing no real ratio argument stands behind the chosen value.

control.req_sample_rate.quantities.sample_rate (a design threshold/minimum) was widened from 100 Hz (journal.jsonl rev 18) to 5 Hz (rev 30), a 20x relaxation, with no issued specification to allow it (policy rule 10: no allowances exist in a no-specification review) and no sourced analysis accompanying the change — only a justification text that itself cites a number (50 Hz) inconsistent with what was written. Per policy rule 6, this widening is unexcused.

control.tilt_estimator.json and control.balance_loop.json (journal.jsonl rev 31, rev 32) both state 'the relaxed 50 Hz minimum,' but the design graph's own control.req_sample_rate.json (rev 30) shows the actual written minimum is 5 Hz, not 50 Hz — a stated claim the revision's own recorded observation directly contradicts.

design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json (and the matching journal.jsonl line, rev 30): torque_peak is recorded as {source: 'derived: [R1.07] * [R2.11] * [R2.26]', unit: 'N*m', value: 219}. Using parts_sheet.json, R1.07 = 0.74 kgf*cm, R2.11 = 148.3 (dimensionless), R2.26 = 2 (dimensionless): 0.74*148.3*2 = 219.48, which is the number recorded, but that number is in kgf*cm, not N*m. Converted correctly (1 kgf*cm = 0.0980665 N*m), the same arithmetic gives 219.48*0.0980665 = 21.5 N*m (3 s.f.), not 219 N*m -- a factor of about 10.2 discrepancy. The two do not agree within half a unit in the third significant figure as the preamble requires, so the written value is inconsistent with its own cited arithmetic in its own declared unit. This is a value the revision wrote (changed source, value and unit together from the prior rev 20 entry), so it is judged on the revision's own work, not excused as a given/unwritten value.

control.balance_loop.torque_peak's recorded source ('derived: [R1.07] * [R2.11] * [R2.26]') does not support its stated value in its declared unit: the arithmetic (0.74*148.3*2=219.48) is in kgf*cm, but the node declares the unit N*m with the same numeric value 219, omitting the ~9.80665x kgf*cm-to-N*m conversion. Per rule 10, 'a value the revision wrote whose recorded source does not support it fails the item as usual.'

control.balance_loop.torque_peak states a derived result of 219 N*m from 'derived: [R1.07] * [R2.11] * [R2.26]', but that arithmetic (0.74 kgf*cm * 148.3 * 2 = 219.48 kgf*cm) converts to 21.5 N*m, not 219 N*m -- the stated/claimed value directly contradicts what its own cited source formula computes once correctly unit-converted.

design/nodes/firmware.imu_driver.json (journal rev 33) writes sample_rate=2000 Hz with source 'design: IMU read rate, one sample per tilt estimator update', but design/nodes/control.tilt_estimator.json (journal rev 32), the very node that source text refers to, writes sample_rate=200 Hz - a stated one-sample-per-update relationship that, before this revision, held exactly (both nodes at 100 Hz, journal revs 19 and 25) and after this revision no longer does (200 Hz vs 2000 Hz, a 10x gap with no new derivation cited). Compounding this, design/nodes/firmware.main.json (rev 34) keeps the source text 'design: scheduler tick at the fastest task rate' at 200 Hz, which is false against the graph's own numbers once firmware.imu_driver's written 2000 Hz is taken at face value (2000 Hz > 200 Hz). All five written nodes keep the required {value, unit, source, written_by} record format, and the Hz unit is used consistently and correctly for all five changed sample_rate quantities, which would otherwise satisfy this item. However, design/nodes/firmware.imu_driver.json (rev 33) records sample_rate=2000 Hz under the unchanged source text 'design: IMU read rate, one sample per tilt estimator update', while design/nodes/control.tilt_estimator.json (rev 32) records sample_rate=200 Hz for 'the tilt estimator update' that source text names. A one-sample-per-update relationship computes to 200 Hz, not 2000 Hz; the recorded source does not support the recorded value, a ten-fold, unexplained departure. This is a magnitude/consistency failure of the kind [rule] and the cross-domain standards' sourcing rule (knowledge/cross/standards.md section 1) exist to catch, and is a rejecting finding under the verdict policy ('a value the revision wrote whose recorded source does not support it fails the item as usual').

design/nodes/firmware.imu_driver.json (rev 33) writes sample_rate=2000 Hz under a source statement ('one sample per tilt estimator update') that, against control.tilt_estimator.json's own written 200 Hz (rev 32), computes to 200 Hz, not 2000 Hz. The design graph itself shows the constant standing in place of what its own cited relationship computes, with no new derivation, measurement, or oversampling source named for the 10x departure, which is exactly [rule]'s observable (a loop rate written into the design state with no measurement, calculation or source behind it, i.e. a source that does not support the value).

mechanical.gearboxes.torque_peak/reaction_moment and control.balance_loop.torque_peak = 240 kgf*cm (derived: [R1a.13]*[R2.12] = 1.1*218.5) double-count the motor's internal 75.81:1 gear reduction, already embedded in the cited stall-torque rating R1a.13, by multiplying again by the overall ratio R2.12 that includes that same internal reduction; and electrical.motors/electrical.power/electrical.motor_drivers still use only the motor's 6V-rated stall current and the pack's nominal 7.2V, never the pack's highest voltage (~8.4V) the standards require for this exact part. electrical.power.supply_voltage, electrical.motor_drivers.supply_voltage and firmware.motor_output.supply_voltage are all recorded only at the nominal 7.2V; no V_max (top of window, ~8.4V for six fresh NiMH cells per electrical/standards.md §4's own worked figure) or V_min (sagged bottom) quantity is declared anywhere in the design graph for the motor branch this revision rewrote.

electrical.motors.stall_current = 1.5A is recorded at the motor's rated 6V (R1a.12) and used directly, unscaled, in electrical.power.motor_current_draw/motor_power_draw; electrical/standards.md §5 and skill.md step 1 give R = V_rated/I_stall = 6/1.5 = 4 ohm and I_stall,max = V_max/R, worked explicitly for this exact motor family to about 2.1A at 8.4V; the revision's written values never perform or record this scaling.

mechanical.gearboxes.torque_peak/reaction_moment = 240 kgf*cm and control.balance_loop.torque_peak = 240 kgf*cm (derived: [R1a.13]*[R2.12] = 1.1 kgf*cm * 218.5 = 240.35, rounds to 240, so the stated arithmetic is reproduced) double-count the motor's internal 75.81:1 gear ratio: R1a.13 is already measured at the gearmotor's geared output shaft, and R2.12 (218.5) is the overall ratio that already includes that same 75.81:1 reduction (218.5/2.88 external-only ratio = R2.02 ~= 75.9 ~= R1a.09=75.81). control.balance_loop.torque_peak was rewritten to 219 kgf*cm via source '[R1.07] * [R2.11] * [R2.26]' (design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json; journal.jsonl rev 30, replacing rev 20's 110 kgf*cm). R1.07 (0.74 kgf*cm, https://www.pololu.com/product/3073/specs) is the Pololu 50:1 Micro Metal Gearmotor's stall torque measured at the gearbox OUTPUT shaft, i.e. already reduced by the motor's own internal ~51.45:1 gear ratio (R1.12). R2.11 (148.3, https://www.pololu.com/file/0J1266/balboa-kit-gear-ratio-chart.pdf) is explicitly the COMBINED internal*external gear ratio for '50:1 gearmotor with 49:17 external gearbox' (51.45*2.88 ~= 148.2). Multiplying R1.07 by R2.11 therefore reapplies the internal 51.45:1 reduction a second time, inflating torque by roughly 51x; a physically consistent combined torque (gearmotor output torque * external-only ratio R2.02=2.88, doubled for two drivetrains via R2.26 or R1.25) would be on the order of 4.3 kgf*cm. The written value of 219 kgf*cm (~21.5 N*m) for a 330 g robot (the node's own 'mass' quantity) is implausible by roughly two orders of magnitude, so the revision is not consistent with the parts sheet's own row definitions or with sound physical reasoning for the design it changes.

This double-counts the motor's internal ~51.45:1 gear stage, inflating the result roughly 51-fold; the physically sound combined torque (gearmotor output * external-only ratio 2.88, doubled for two drivetrains) is on the order of 4.3 kgf*cm, not 219. Scrutinised by reading (cross-domain standards section 7; [rule]'s mandate not to treat a passed-looking number as correct), this magnitude is implausible by roughly two orders of magnitude for a 330 g robot.

This is a written-value defect decidable purely by reading the record (no additional unwritten computation is needed to see the metric is unnamed), so it is a fail under the Unwritten-records carve-out ('a check that involves a written value, that the values on the page decide by reading, and that fails, is judged normally'). Skill 'estimating driver junction temperature' step 4 and standards.md §6 both require the metric to be named because RθJA and RθJB are not interchangeable in TJ = T_reference x P: RθJA pairs with ambient temperature, RθJB pairs with a measured board temperature, and conflating them would understate a real TJ estimate.

The two records that both purport to state the total mass of the balancing robot (assembly.mass = 365 g vs. balance_loop.plant_mass = 330 g) now disagree by the exact mass of the part just added (35 g), and firmware.balance_task's new `no_change_justified` text ("Only the plant mass in the loop changed") falsely asserts that plant_mass changed when the written record shows it did not. This is an unresolved, self-contradictory state written by the revision itself, not a condition inherited unchanged from a given value.

control.balance_loop.plant_mass (330 g, unchanged) no longer agrees with the mass of the system it is supposed to track: mechanical.assembly.mass, which the revision wrote to 365 g, constrains control.balance_loop and represents the same total-robot-mass quantity. The two values now disagree by 35 g (the bumper cage just added), a magnitude mismatch against the dependent value the design itself names (cross §5; std §11).

mechanical.assembly.mass is a physically-different, written change (330 g -> 365 g, journal rev 31) and mechanical.assembly `constrains` control.balance_loop. control.balance_loop was rewritten (journal rev 32) but its plant_mass value/source are byte-identical to the prior revision (journal rev 21) -- no follow-up change was made, and no `no_change_justified` entry exists on control.balance_loop for this edge. The only no_change_justified text in the delivered work is on firmware.balance_task and is keyed to control.balance_loop, asserting the plant mass changed -- which the control.balance_loop record itself contradicts. The mechanical.bumper_cage -> mechanical.chassis and mechanical.chassis -> mechanical.assembly edges, by contrast, were followed up correctly (+35 g propagated at each step).

firmware.balance_task's new no_change_justified entry states 'Only the plant mass in the loop changed; the loop rate ... are unchanged,' asserting that control.balance_loop's plant_mass changed. The written control.balance_loop.json payload (compare journal rev 21 and rev 32, and the diff hunk for design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json) shows plant_mass unchanged at 330 g with the identical source string. The claim directly contradicts the data it cites, and the no_change_justified text is a value the revision itself wrote.

The revision is not consistent with the design it changes or with the rubric: it re-saved firmware.motor_output.pwm_duty_limit unchanged (still keyed to the old NiMH pack-voltage row R5.03) after raising electrical.battery_pack.supply_voltage from 7.2 V to 9 V, which lets the motor see 7.5 V average against its 6 V rating (design/nodes/firmware.motor_output.json rev 33 vs electrical.battery_pack.json rev 30); it uses a physically incorrect power-conservation formula instead of Ohm's-law scaling for motor stall current (electrical.battery_pack.json motor_current_draw, electrical.driver_left.json / electrical.driver_right.json current_draw); it drops the only capacity/mass data the battery cell had without sourcing alkaline-specific replacements (design/nodes/electrical.battery_cell.json, electrical.battery_pack.json); and it checks the battery rail only at the single nominal voltage, never at the window's top or sagged bottom.

The revision replaces the battery cell's chemistry (electrical.battery_cell.json: rated_voltage source changed from a specific NiMH product page, pololu.com/product/1003/specs, 1.2 V, to a derived 1.5 V alkaline figure sourced only to the generic Balboa guide page). No manufacturer part number or cell-specific datasheet for the new alkaline cell is recorded anywhere in the node, and charge_capacity and mass_per_cell (the only part-identifying ratings the old NiMH cell record carried) were deleted with no alkaline replacement. Per the rubric, sourcing a changed part's rating/part-number is the revision's own duty (Missing Evidence, [rule] example), so this is a finding, not a blocked or excused gap.

No continuous or peak/current-limit rating for the battery pack itself is present in the design after the revision: the prior charge_capacity (2.2 A*h, electrical.battery_pack.json rev 10) was deleted and no alkaline-sourced discharge-rate or capacity limit was supplied to replace it, so the budget cannot be shown to 'close' against any supply-side rating. On the driver side, the figure being compared (current_draw = 1.0 A per driver) rests on the flawed power/voltage formula identified under [rule], so even that partial closure is unreliable. [rule] is one of the rubric's explicit findings-as-usual items regardless of what records the revision wrote, and it fails here.

electrical.battery_cell.json names no alkaline cell part and cites no manufacturer maximum discharge rate; electrical.battery_pack.json's motor_current_draw (2.0 A, flawed per [rule] besides) is never compared against any sourced alkaline discharge-rate limit or published discharge-curve evidence, as the standards require for a chemistry with no library-held C-rate (section 3). The cell type here is chosen and changed by the revision itself (NiMH -> alkaline), so the [B: cell type] marker does not block this: naming the cell and sourcing its discharge limit is the revision's own duty, and it was not done.

electrical.battery_pack.json (motor_current_draw, motor_power_draw), electrical.driver_left.json and electrical.driver_right.json (current_draw) are all re-derived using only the single nominal pack voltage from R5.04 (9 V); no check is shown at the top of the window (highest open-circuit voltage of six fresh alkaline cells, above 9 V) or at the sagged bottom under load. This is a written value re-computed by the revision, so it is judged normally and fails.

electrical.battery_pack.json motor_current_draw = [R1.02]*[R1.04]*[R4.19]/[R5.04] = 6 V * 1.5 A * 2 / 9 V = 2.0 A, and electrical.driver_left/right.json current_draw = [R1.02]*[R1.04]/[R5.04] = 6*1.5/9 = 1.0 A per driver. This takes the motor's stall power AT ITS RATED VOLTAGE (6 V * 1.5 A = 9 W per motor) and divides by the pack voltage (9 V) to get a 'current', which assumes constant power with voltage. The standards' required method is Ohm's-law scaling: R = V_rated/I_stall = 6/1.5 = 4 Ohm, I_stall,max = V_pack/R = 9/4 = 2.25 A per motor (4.5 A for two). The design's figure (1.0 A per driver, 2.0 A total) understates the true stall-current bound by more than a factor of two.

Because the stall-current figure feeding this comparison is wrong (see [rule]), the recorded comparison (current_draw 1.0 A per driver vs current_limit 1.8 A) hides a real exceedance: the correctly-scaled stall current (~2.25 A per motor) is above both the 1.8 A peak rating and the 1.9 A minimum OCP trip, which the design never states or declares to the control/firmware roles as the standard requires.

electrical.battery_pack.json's supply_voltage changed from 7.2 V to 9 V (rev 10 -> rev 30), and it constrains firmware.motor_output. firmware.motor_output.json was rewritten in the same change set (rev 27 -> rev 33) but its pwm_duty_limit value (0.833) and formula ([R1.02]/[R5.03]) are byte-identical to before: it still divides by R5.03 (the old 7.2 V NiMH row), not R5.04 (the new 9 V alkaline row). This is a re-saved identical number with a stale source, not a genuine follow-up, and no no_change_justified reason was recorded for this edge. Read together, 0.833 * 9 V = 7.5 V > the motor's 6 V rated voltage (R1.02), a real overvoltage the stale follow-up lets through.

electrical.battery_pack.json, electrical.driver_left.json and electrical.driver_right.json current/power figures are all computed solely at the single nominal pack voltage (R5.04, 9 V); no check is shown at the charged top or sagged bottom of the six-alkaline-cell window, matching the 'one battery voltage' antipattern exactly.

The stall current feeding the driver comparison is not properly derived via Ohm's-law scaling to the pack's highest voltage; it is instead computed from a power figure taken at the motor's rated voltage and divided by the pack voltage, producing an under-scaled result. The practical effect matches the antipattern's concern (stall current not correctly referred to the pack's own voltage).

electrical.battery_pack.supply_voltage (9 V, written) and firmware.motor_output.pwm_duty_limit (0.833, re-saved with a stale 7.2 V-keyed formula) are each self-consistent with their own stated formulas in isolation, but read together (0.833*9 V = 7.5 V) they exceed the motor's 6 V rating (R1.02); the combination the standards require (the PWM ceiling checked against the actual pack voltage) was never performed across the two nodes in the final state.

design/nodes/electrical.imu.json (rev 30, version 2) keeps current_draw at 0.9 mA (the LSM6DS33 normal-mode figure, R8.05) even though firmware.imu_driver's own written rationale in design/nodes/firmware.imu_driver.json (sample_rate 416 Hz, source: '...requires high-performance mode') and electrical.control_board's own re-derivation in design/nodes/electrical.control_board.json (sensor_power_draw 4.13 mW = R8.03*R8.04, the high-performance-mode current row, 1.25 mA) both depend on the IMU now running in high-performance mode. control.balance_loop's written no_change_justified text in design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json asserts 'the IMU's supply current changed,' which the electrical.imu node itself contradicts by recording no change. The revision's written values are therefore mutually inconsistent.

firmware.imu_driver.sample_rate changed from 208 Hz to 416 Hz (design/journal.jsonl rev 29) and constrains electrical.imu. electrical.imu was touched by this revision (rev 30, version 2) but its current_draw quantity was left at the stale normal-mode value (0.9 mA, design/nodes/electrical.imu.json) instead of being updated to the high-performance-mode value (1.25 mA, R8.04) that the revision's own stated rationale and electrical.control_board's own updated derivation (design/nodes/electrical.control_board.json, 4.13 mW = R8.03*R8.04) both require. The follow-up is present in form (a journal write) but, read on its merits, does not actually hold, which [rule] requires beyond mere presence.

design/nodes/electrical.imu.json's 'current_draw' quantity is written as {value: 1.25, unit: 'mW', source: 'https://www.pololu.com/file/0J1087/LSM6DS33.pdf'}. parts_sheet.json row R8.04 ('supply current, gyro + accel high-performance mode') gives 1.25 mA, not 1.25 mW; the revision copied the milliamp figure into a field now labelled in milliwatts without converting it (3.3 V x 1.25 mA = 4.125 mW, which is the separate value correctly written to electrical.control_board.sensor_power_draw, not to electrical.imu.current_draw). A quantity named 'current_draw' cannot physically carry a power unit. This is a written-value inconsistency internal to the revision, so the single consistency line is unmet.

design/nodes/electrical.imu.json's current_draw quantity is recorded as {value: 1.25, unit: 'mW', source: LSM6DS33.pdf}, but 1.25 is parts_sheet.json row R8.04's current in mA (1.25 mA, high-performance mode); the figure was carried over without the V*I conversion that would actually produce a milliwatt figure (3.3 V x 1.25 mA = 4.125 mW, the value correctly written elsewhere to electrical.control_board.sensor_power_draw). A quantity named 'current_draw' cannot carry a watt-dimensioned unit; this is a unit-kind mismatch in a quantity the revision itself wrote, which [rule]'s record-format and unit-consistency requirement is meant to catch.

design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json's sample_rate was rewritten from 100 Hz to 400 Hz with the new source, design: 2.5 ms control period, reducing sampling delay in the tilt loop, above the required minimum loop rate (diff hunk against design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json). This text states no ratio of 400 Hz to the delivered loop's crossover frequency or closed-loop bandwidth, it only compares the new rate qualitatively to the 100 Hz floor in control.req_loop_rate.json, which is the antipattern [rule] names: a round-number sample rate, 400 Hz is exactly 4x the stated floor, justified by a generic appeal to being above the minimum and reducing delay rather than an argued ratio to the achieved bandwidth.

The revision is inconsistent with the design it changes. control.balance_loop's new no_change_justified text (design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json; journal.jsonl rev30) asserts the gain change 'does not change... the actuator torque and speed limits the motors and gearboxes set,' yet the very same write changed control.balance_loop's own torque_peak quantity from 0.145 N*m (source 'derived: [R1.07] * [R1.25]') to 0.0726 N*m (source the Pololu 3073 spec page) - i.e. the actuator torque limit the node itself declares was halved by this revision. That change was never propagated or justified to firmware.balance_task, which control.balance_loop constrains (see [rule]). The written justification is therefore false as applied to the revision's own edit, and a required propagation step is missing.

control.balance_loop's torque_peak quantity changed physically (0.145 N*m -> 0.0726 N*m, diff hunk for design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json; journal.jsonl rev30) and control.balance_loop constrains firmware.balance_task (its 'constrains' list). firmware.balance_task was not written in this revision and carries no no_change_justified entry keyed to 'control.balance_loop' explaining why the halved torque_peak needs no change there; the only no_change_justified entry present is keyed to 'control.angle_controller' and addresses the gain change into balance_loop, not the torque_peak change out of balance_loop. The follow-up this change owes to firmware.balance_task is missing entirely.

control.balance_loop's no_change_justified text states that the gain change 'does not change... the actuator torque and speed limits the motors and gearboxes set,' yet the same write changed control.balance_loop's own torque_peak from 0.145 N*m to 0.0726 N*m (journal.jsonl rev30; design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json) - a stated result directly contradicted by the revision's own written artefact.

design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json (and journal.jsonl rev 30 vs rev 21) show plant_mass changed from 330 g ('derived: [R11.01] - [R10.03] + [R5.07] * [R5.10]') to 165 g ('derived: [R11.01] - [R10.03]') in the same write that adds the no_change_justified text 'A gain inside the loop does not change its sample rate, the plant mass or the actuator torque and speed limits the motors and gearboxes set.' The claim that the plant mass is unaffected is directly contradicted by the write's own payload, which halves it by removing the ~165 g battery-pack term (matching electrical.battery_pack.mass = 165 g, R5.07(0.97 oz≈27.5 g)×R5.10(6 cells)=165 g). mechanical.assembly.mass, the design's own canonical laden mass, remains 330 g (unwritten, given), so control.balance_loop's plant_mass now disagrees with the mechanical domain's figure for the same physical robot with no stated reason. This is an unexplained, self-contradictory, and physically consequential change (it understates the inverted-pendulum's true tipping mass by roughly half) bundled into what is presented as an isolated gain adjustment, so the revision is not consistent with the design it changes.

control.balance_loop's plant_mass changed from 330 g to 165 g in this revision (design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json; journal.jsonl rev 30 vs rev 21) — a physically different value, not a re-save. control.balance_loop's own 'constrains' field names firmware.balance_task, which received no follow-up change in this changeset, and no no_change_justified entry addresses plant_mass or firmware.balance_task at all (the one no_change_justified entry present is keyed to control.rate_controller and, moreover, denies that the plant mass changed). The changed quantity therefore did not reach the node it constrains, and carries no stated reason that it needed none.

control.balance_loop's plant_mass was moved from its established, sourced value of 330 g (set at node creation, journal rev 21, 'derived: [R11.01] - [R10.03] + [R5.07] * [R5.10]', matching mechanical.assembly.mass = 330 g, itself tracking the ~165 g battery pack via electrical.battery_pack.mass) down to 165 g ('derived: [R11.01] - [R10.03]'), dropping the battery-pack mass term entirely with no sourced engineering rationale for doing so. No issued specification exists to supply an allowance (policy rule 10: 'With no issued specification there are no allowances'), so this plant-parameter departure is not excused.

design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json's no_change_justified field states 'A gain inside the loop does not change its sample rate, the plant mass or the actuator torque and speed limits the motors and gearboxes set,' yet the very same write's quantities block shows plant_mass changed from 330 g to 165 g (journal.jsonl rev 30 vs rev 21) — the stated claim is directly contradicted by the observation of the written payload itself.

control.balance_loop's new torque_limit (design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json, journal.jsonl rev 29) is recorded as 0.32 N*m from 'derived: [R1.18] * [R1.25]'. Reading parts_sheet.json: R1.18 = 0.16 kilogram_force*cm, R1.25 = 2 (dimensionless); the arithmetic gives 0.32 kilogram_force*cm, which converts to 0.32*0.0980665 ≈ 0.0314 N*m -- not 0.32 N*m. The same node's own torque_peak field (derived: [R1.07]*[R1.25] = 0.74*2 = 1.48 kgf*cm -> 1.48*0.0980665 ≈ 0.145 N*m) and plant_mass field (correctly converting R5.07's ounces to grams) show the design's established practice is to convert units before recording; torque_limit fails to do so, making the revision inconsistent with the design it changes.

control.balance_loop's torque_limit is recorded as 0.32 N*m from 'derived: [R1.18] * [R1.25]'. Reading parts_sheet.json rows R1.18 (0.16 kilogram_force*cm) and R1.25 (2, dimensionless) gives 0.32 kilogram_force*cm, which converts to 0.32*0.0980665 ≈ 0.0314 N*m, not 0.32 N*m -- the source cited does not support the value recorded in its stated unit, unlike the node's own torque_peak field which performs the same conversion correctly (0.74*2=1.48 kgf*cm -> 0.145 N*m, matching what is recorded).

control.balance_loop's torque_limit record claims the value 0.32 N*m is the result of 'derived: [R1.18] * [R1.25]'; reading R1.18 (0.16 kilogram_force*cm) and R1.25 (2) and performing that arithmetic with the unit conversion the design itself uses elsewhere (torque_peak, plant_mass) gives 0.0314 N*m, which the stated 0.32 N*m contradicts.

The revision writes control.balance_loop's new 'speed_limit' quantity as {value: 513, unit: 'rad/s', source: 'https://www.pololu.com/product/3073/specs', written_by: 'control'} (design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json; design/journal.jsonl rev 29). That exact URL is already used, in the same node, for 'no_load_speed' = 68.1 rad/s, and the project's own parts sheet (parts_sheet.json, row R1.10, 'no-load speed @ 6V' = 650 rpm, same URL) converts to 68.1 rad/s (650 x 2pi/60 ~= 68.07), matching the existing field exactly. No row of parts_sheet.json, and no arithmetic over its rows, yields 513 rad/s (~4900 rpm) by any unit conversion, and the field carries a bare URL (not a 'derived: ...' expression) implying a direct copy. This written value is inconsistent with the design's own stated convention ('a number copied from a row of the parts sheet is that row's number, converted only between units') and with rule 10's Evidence clause ('a value the revision wrote whose recorded source does not support it fails the item as usual').

The actuator magnitude limit (control.balance_loop's pre-existing 'torque_peak' = 0.145 N*m) and, after this revision, a rate limit ('speed_limit' = 513 rad/s) are both present as quantity records, so the [B] missing-input triggers for 'no magnitude/rate limit' are resolved. But the newly declared rate limit is not a legitimate declaration: its value is not supported by its own cited source (see [rule]'s evidence -- the same URL's own extracted figure, parts_sheet.json row R1.10, gives 68.1 rad/s, not 513). A declaration carrying a source that does not actually support the number it reports does not satisfy the standards' sourcing discipline (knowledge/cross/standards.md SS1: a source exists so 'the next role, the reviewer, and the gate's own magnitude check...need to know where a number claims to come from'), so the rate limit is not properly declared. No integral action is evidenced anywhere ([rule]/[rule]/[rule]), so the anti-windup naming sub-check does not trigger.

The revision states, as a sourced fact, that control.balance_loop's 'speed_limit' = 513 rad/s comes from https://www.pololu.com/product/3073/specs (design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json; design/journal.jsonl rev 29) -- the identical URL the same node already cites for 'no_load_speed' = 68.1 rad/s. The design's own evidentiary record of that URL, parts_sheet.json row R1.10 ('no-load speed @ 6V', 650 rpm, same URL), converts to 68.1 rad/s (650 x 2pi/60 ~= 68.07), contradicting the stated 513 rad/s; no other row of parts_sheet.json, alone or in any arithmetic combination, produces 513 rad/s either. The stated result (513 rad/s, sourced to that page) is contradicted by the one observation available of what that page actually gives (68.1 rad/s, R1.10).

electrical.motor_left's written efficiency_point_output_power carries unit 'J' instead of 'W' (journal rev 29), inconsistent with the identical field on electrical.motor_right (rev 30, unit 'W', same source and value 0.8); and the written no_change_justified text on electrical.driver_left/right (revs 31-32) asserts driver adequacy using only the motor's rated-voltage (6 V) stall current (1.5 A), without the pack's-highest-voltage scaling that the electrical standards file's own worked example (identical motor and DRV8838 driver) shows fails (~2.1 A at 8.4 V versus the 1.8 A current_limit recorded here), with no declaration of the stall-trip condition to control/firmware. Both are the revision's own written content, not inherited given values, so the revision is not consistent with itself or with the standards it is held to.

The newly written no_change_justified text on electrical.driver_left/driver_right (journal revs 31-32) relies on the motor's rated-voltage stall current (1.5 A at 6 V, electrical.motor_left/right quantities, unchanged) as sufficient justification that the driver remains adequately sized, with no I_stall,max = V_max/R bound computed at the pack's higher voltage (nominal 7.2 V, electrical.battery_pack rev 10, let alone the charged top of the window). Per §5 and the electrical standards file's own worked example for this identical 6 V/1.5 A Pololu gearmotor and DRV8838 driver, the correctly scaled stall current reaches about 2.1 A at 8.4 V -- 'use of the rated-voltage figure at a higher supply fails,' and that is exactly what the written claim does.

electrical.driver_left/right record only a single current figure, 'current_limit' = 1.8 A (journal revs 31-32, unchanged from rev 13-14), not the three required comparisons (continuous rating, peak rating, minimum OCP trip). The revision's new written claim ('lies well inside it') does not supply or reference the missing minimum-OCP-trip and continuous-rating comparisons, and does not state the driver's behaviour or declare the stall-trip condition to control/firmware as required when the trip is exceeded, which -- per the standards file's worked example for this exact pairing -- it is at the pack's higher voltage.

electrical.motor_left's written efficiency_point_output_power (journal rev 29) carries unit 'J' (a unit of energy) for a quantity representing output power (parts-sheet row R1.20, 0.8 W), while the identical field on electrical.motor_right (rev 30), same source and value 0.8, is correctly recorded as 'W'. This is a unit-kind mismatch -- the gate's own distinction of kinds (cross-domain standards §2) -- and fails [rule]'s 'unit arithmetic that does not balance' criterion (cat. 1).

The revision's newly written no_change_justified text on electrical.driver_left/driver_right states the driver 'is sized for the 1.5 A stall current' (the motor's rated-voltage, 6 V, stall figure) and that the 0.42 A efficiency-point current 'lies well inside it,' with no mention of the pack's higher voltage (nominal 7.2 V, higher still when fresh). This is exactly the rated-voltage-stall-current-vs-driver comparison the antipattern describes, while the pack voltage is admittedly higher than the motor's 6 V rating.

The newly written no_change_justified text on electrical.driver_left/driver_right passes the visible [rule] follow-up obligation by citing only the rated-voltage (6 V) stall current (1.5 A) as the sizing basis -- the easy, 'visible' condition -- while the standards-required check at the pack's actual higher voltage (which the electrical standards file's own worked example for this identical 6 V/1.5 A Pololu gearmotor and DRV8838 driver shows reaches about 2.1 A at 8.4 V, above the 1.8 A current_limit and 1.9 A trip recorded here) was not performed. The failing check turns on the written no_change_justified claim, which is what closes out the follow-up obligation at the easier condition.

design/nodes/electrical.control_board.json (journal.jsonl rev 31) records sensor_power_draw as {unit: 'W', value: 4.13, source: 'derived: [R8.03] * [R8.04]'}. [R8.03] (parts_sheet.json, row R8.03) = 3.3 V and [R8.04] = 1.25 mA, so the arithmetic 3.3 V x 1.25 mA = 4.125 mW, not 4.125 W -- the unit is wrong by a factor of 1000. This written value is also inconsistent with the revision's own follow-up at design/nodes/electrical.regulator_5v.json (rev 32), whose no_change_justified text for electrical.control_board says 'The sensor's rise of about 1.2 mW is negligible' -- a description that matches the correct mW-scale rise (4.13 mW - 2.97 mW = 1.16 mW) but directly contradicts the 4.13 W the control-board node itself now states (an actual rise of about 1.16 W, which is neither 'about 1.2 mW' nor negligible against a 2 A/5 V, 10 W regulator). The revision is therefore not internally consistent.

design/nodes/electrical.control_board.json (journal.jsonl rev 31, line 11 of diff-01-of-01.patch) records sensor_power_draw as {value: 4.13, unit: 'W', source: 'derived: [R8.03] * [R8.04]'}. parts_sheet.json gives R8.03 = 3.3 V (row R8.03, 'supply on board') and R8.04 = 1.25 mA (row R8.04, 'supply current, gyro + accel high-performance mode'). V x mA = mW, so the arithmetic yields 4.125 mW, which rounds to the recorded value 4.13 -- but the unit field says 'W', a 1000x error. This is a unit-arithmetic/conversion error in a design-state quantity record, a finding under [rule] regardless of the value's given/written status, since a unit error is explicitly one of the checks 'not touched by' the given-value exception.

Each changed quantity's constrains edge received a follow-up or a stated reason: firmware.imu_driver -> electrical.imu (current_draw updated, journal rev 30); electrical.imu -> electrical.control_board (sensor_power_draw updated, rev 31) and -> control.balance_loop (no_change_justified added, rev 33, whose reasoning holds -- the loop's 100 Hz rate, plant mass and actuator figures genuinely do not depend on the sensor's supply current); electrical.control_board -> electrical.regulator_5v (no_change_justified added, rev 32). However, that last follow-up's stated reason does not actually hold by reading: design/nodes/electrical.regulator_5v.json says 'The sensor's rise of about 1.2 mW is negligible against the regulator's 2 A rating,' but design/nodes/electrical.control_board.json's own recorded value for the same quantity is 4.13 W, implying a rise of about 1.16 W (not 1.2 mW) against a 5 V/2 A = 10 W regulator -- not negligible on the record's own terms. [rule] requires judging 'whether a stated reason actually holds,' and by the revision's own written figures it does not.

design/nodes/control.req_loop_rate.json writes quantities.sample_rate.value = 5 (unit Hz), but design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json's new no_change_justified.control.req_loop_rate field reads 'The 100 Hz loop already exceeds the relaxed 50 Hz minimum...' - citing 50 Hz as the minimum when the sibling record the same change set wrote states 5 Hz (journal.jsonl rev 29 and rev 30, both dated 2026-09-28T10:00:00Z). The revision's own written records contradict each other by a factor of 10, so it is not consistent with the design it changes.

control.req_loop_rate.sample_rate changed (100→5 Hz) and this node 'constrains' control.balance_loop, so a follow-up is owed. The follow-up given (no_change_justified on control.balance_loop) cites 'the relaxed 50 Hz minimum' as the reason no change is needed, but the value actually written in the same change set is 5 Hz, not 50 Hz (journal.jsonl rev 29). A propagation reason that misstates the governing quantity it is reasoning from is not a valid justification, even though the underlying conclusion (100 Hz exceeds the stated floor) happens to hold under either number.

journal.jsonl rev 29 / design/nodes/control.req_loop_rate.json: sample_rate changed from 100 Hz to 5 Hz, a 20x widening of the design's own minimum-loop-rate requirement, justified only as 'relaxed to admit slower test builds' with no sourced stability analysis establishing 5 Hz is adequate for an inherently unstable plant.

control.balance_loop's no_change_justified text states 'the relaxed 50 Hz minimum,' but the design graph's own record (control.req_loop_rate.json, written in the same change set) shows sample_rate = 5 Hz, not 50 Hz - the design graph itself (the observation, per policy rule 10) directly contradicts the stated claim.
