control.balance_loop (rev 29) added torque_limit and a new constrains edge to electrical.driver_left/right; electrical.battery_pack (rev 33) added continuous_motor_current_draw/continuous_motor_power_draw, constraining mechanical.assembly, firmware.motor_output, electrical.driver_left and electrical.driver_right. mechanical.assembly, firmware.motor_output and firmware.balance_task each received a specific no_change_justified reason (design/nodes/mechanical.assembly.json rev 34, design/nodes/firmware.motor_output.json rev 35, design/nodes/firmware.balance_task.json rev 30), and electrical.driver_right received an actual follow-up quantity change (design/nodes/electrical.driver_right.json rev 32). electrical.driver_left (design/nodes/electrical.driver_left.json rev 31) received neither: its payload is unchanged from rev 13 and carries no no_change_justified key at all.

firmware.fall_detector.json (new node) records quantities.sample_rate = {value: 13, unit: 'Hz', source: 'design: lowest LSM6DS33 output data rate, used in low-power mode to watch for the robot being stood up while it lies fallen'}. The LSM6DS33's actual lowest active output data rate (its low-power-mode-only setting) is 12.5 Hz, not 13 Hz -- confirmed by the design's own, unchanged firmware.imu_driver.json node, which correctly cites 208 Hz (a genuine entry in the same chip's ODR table: 12.5/26/52/104/208/416/833/1660/3330/6660 Hz) as the 'highest LSM6DS33 normal-mode output data rate'. 13 Hz is not an entry in that table and is not three-significant-figure rounding of 12.5 (which already has three significant figures). The written value is therefore inconsistent with the physical fact its own cited source names, even though the rest of the revision (the no_change_justified entries on electrical.control_board and control.balance_loop, and electrical.imu's unchanged current_draw/supply_voltage) is internally consistent and well-reasoned.

Every quantity record written by this revision has the required {value, unit, source, written_by} shape, and the unit for firmware.fall_detector.sample_rate (Hz, a frequency) is correctly not confused with rad/s. However, the magnitude itself is unsupported by its stated source: firmware.fall_detector.json records sample_rate = 13 Hz as 'the lowest LSM6DS33 output data rate', but the LSM6DS33's real lowest active ODR (its low-power-mode setting) is 12.5 Hz -- a figure corroborated by this same design's unchanged firmware.imu_driver node, which correctly cites 208 Hz (a genuine table entry for the same chip) elsewhere. 13 Hz does not appear in the chip's real ODR table and is not a defensible rounding of 12.5 Hz.

The revision is not consistent with the design it changes and with this rubric: electrical.control_board (design/nodes/electrical.control_board.json, journal rev 29) added mechanical.chassis to its constrains edges while adding new board_length/board_width/board_thickness quantities, but mechanical.chassis (design/nodes/mechanical.chassis.json, journal rev 31) was rewritten in the same changeset with every quantity (mass 165 g, reaction_moment 0.145 N*m, track_width 102 mm) and geometry_hash byte-identical to its prior revision (rev 4), and carries no no_change_justified entry naming electrical.control_board. None of [rule]'s three required conditions (a real change, a specific no_change_justified reason, or a named owed follow-up) is satisfied for this edge, which fails [rule] (cross §5) and is a rejecting finding.

electrical.control_board (design/nodes/electrical.control_board.json, journal rev 29) altered quantities (added board_length/board_width/board_thickness) and added mechanical.chassis to its constrains edges. For the pre-existing edge to electrical.regulator_5v, a specific no_change_justified reason is given (design/nodes/electrical.regulator_5v.json, journal rev 30) and this satisfies [rule] for that edge. But for the new edge to mechanical.chassis, chassis's own node (design/nodes/mechanical.chassis.json, journal rev 31, version 2) is byte-identical in every field (mass 165 g, reaction_moment 0.145 N*m, track_width 102 mm, geometry_hash) to its prior revision (rev 4, version 1) -- a re-saved identical value, which cross §5 excludes from counting as a change -- and chassis carries no no_change_justified entry naming electrical.control_board, nor does any node name a future owed follow-up for this edge. None of [rule]'s three disjuncts is satisfied for mechanical.chassis, so [rule] fails for this edge. This is a new defect (the edge did not exist in the base design before this revision), not a pre-existing condition excused by the form-2 'conditions already in the design' rule.

mechanical.assembly's no_change_justified entry (design/nodes/mechanical.assembly.json, journal rev 32) states 'Only a fit clearance was added to the chassis,' but mechanical.chassis's own record (design/nodes/mechanical.chassis.json, journal rev 31) shows no such addition: every field, including geometry_hash and all three quantities, is byte-identical to the prior revision (rev 4). This is a claim the revision wrote with no corroborating record anywhere in the design graph.

The revision is not consistent with the design it changes: control.tilt_estimator (design/nodes/control.tilt_estimator.json) states the complementary filter runs 'at an LSM6DS33 output data rate above four times the 100 Hz loop rate' (416 Hz) and lists firmware.imu_driver in its constrains edge, implying the IMU driver must supply samples at that rate; but firmware.imu_driver (design/nodes/firmware.imu_driver.json; journal.jsonl rev 30) was rewritten with the identical prior value (208 Hz) and identical prior source text ('highest LSM6DS33 normal-mode output data rate, above twice the balance-task rate'), with no no_change_justified entry reconciling the two. The electrical domain's own parallel change (electrical.imu.current_draw raised from 0.9 mA, R8.05/normal-mode, to 1.25 mA, R8.04/high-performance-mode) corroborates that a real operating-mode/rate change was intended, making firmware.imu_driver's unchanged 'normal-mode, 208 Hz' statement a live contradiction left unresolved by the revision.

control.tilt_estimator's new sample_rate quantity (416 Hz) carries a constrains edge to both control.balance_loop and firmware.imu_driver (design/nodes/control.tilt_estimator.json). The control.balance_loop edge is properly handled with a no_change_justified reason (design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json). The firmware.imu_driver edge is not: firmware.imu_driver was rewritten (journal.jsonl rev 30; diff-01-of-01.patch lines 59-67) with the identical prior value (208 Hz) and identical prior source text, and carries no no_change_justified entry explaining why a node whose own description ('highest...normal-mode...rate') is numerically and qualitatively inconsistent with the newly-stated 416 Hz/high-performance-mode requirement needs no change. This is a missed follow-up under cross-domain standard 5, and because control.tilt_estimator is a value the revision added (no base-state analogue), it is not excused as a condition 'already in the design'.

design/nodes/mechanical.gearbox_left.json (and journal.jsonl rev 31) show the node the revision itself newly added to control.balance_loop's constrains list was rewritten with no quantity change and no no_change_justified entry, while its structural twin mechanical.gearbox_right.json (journal rev 32) received the matching 'input_speed_limit' quantity -- an asymmetric, unjustified gap the revision created in its own propagation. Additionally, the new 'speed_limit'/'input_speed_limit' value (51.3 rad/s) matches parts_sheet.json row R1.17 ('speed at max efficiency', 490 rpm) rather than any stated speed limit, a mismatch between the quantity's name and its apparent source that the revision does not explain. Both make the revision inconsistent with itself.

control.balance_loop added the quantity speed_limit and newly listed mechanical.gearbox_left and mechanical.gearbox_right in its 'constrains' array (design/journal.jsonl rev 29, compare rev 21). mechanical.gearbox_right received a follow-up quantity, input_speed_limit = 51.3 rad/s (rev 32). mechanical.gearbox_left (rev 31) received neither a follow-up quantity nor a no_change_justified entry -- its payload is identical to its pre-revision state (rev 5). Since this constrains edge to gearbox_left did not exist before the revision (the base control.balance_loop.constrains held only firmware.balance_task), the 'conditions already in the design' carve-out in the rubric's Section 2 preamble does not apply: this is a new obligation the revision itself created and did not discharge.

The revision's single consistency line fails: design/nodes/electrical.imu.json's new quantity standby_current_draw is written as {value: 6, unit: 'mA', source: 'https://www.pololu.com/file/0J1087/LSM6DS33.pdf'}, citing the exact URL of parts_sheet.json row R8.08 ('power-down current', value 6, unit 'uA'). The journal preamble states a number copied from a parts-sheet row is that row's number 'converted only between units' -- 6 uA is 0.006 mA, not 6 mA -- so the written value is inconsistent with its own cited source by a factor of 1000, breaking the design's own stated numbering rule and the rubric's unit-correctness requirement ([rule]).

design/nodes/electrical.imu.json's new quantity standby_current_draw records {value: 6, unit: 'mA', source: '.../LSM6DS33.pdf'}, but that exact URL in parts_sheet.json is row R8.08 ('power-down current', value 6, unit 'uA'); 6 uA is 0.006 mA, so the written record is off by a factor of 1000 from the datasheet figure it cites. This is a unit/magnitude error in a design-state quantity record, which [rule] (and the design's own numbering rule in the journal preamble, 'converted only between units') requires to be correct; it is not shielded by the given-value or conditions-already-in-the-design rules because the field is newly written by this revision (absent from the prior rev 17 of electrical.imu) and because [rule]-type unit errors are explicitly judged on the values present regardless.

mechanical.chassis.mass changed from 165 g (journal.jsonl line 4, rev4) to 205 g (journal.jsonl line 29, rev29) via a formula that double-counts the wheel-pair mass already contained in [R11.01]-[R10.03] (proved by mechanical.frame_and_board.mass=106g, journal.jsonl line 7, and mechanical.wheel_pair.mass=39.7g, journal.jsonl line 8, and motor masses 9.5g each, journal.jsonl lines 11-12, which sum to the chassis's own prior value of 165g). The accompanying no_change_justified entry added to mechanical.assembly (journal.jsonl line 30) claims the mass is unchanged because 'no part was added or moved', which is contradicted by the 40 g change in chassis.mass that this very revision produced. The revision is therefore not consistent with the design it changes.

mechanical.chassis.mass is written as 205g (design/nodes/mechanical.chassis.json; journal.jsonl line 29) via a formula that adds the wheel-pair mass term '[R9.03]*[R9.06]' to a base ([R11.01]-[R10.03]) that already includes the wheel-pair mass once, as proven by mechanical.frame_and_board.mass=106g (journal.jsonl line 7, formula '[R11.01]-[R10.03]-[R9.03]*[R9.06]-[R1.21]*[R1.25]') and mechanical.wheel_pair.mass=39.7g (journal.jsonl line 8) and the two 9.5g motor masses (journal.jsonl lines 11-12), which together sum to 164.7g ≈ the chassis's own pre-revision value of 165g (journal.jsonl line 4). The new 205g value is therefore inconsistent with its neighbouring, already-sourced component masses by about 40g (24%), confirmed further by the skill file's worked example stating R11.01's 200g is 'assembled with motors, 80 mm wheels and bumper cage' (knowledge/mechanical/skill.md).

mechanical.chassis has a constrains edge to mechanical.assembly (design/nodes/mechanical.chassis.json, 'constrains':['mechanical.assembly']) and its mass quantity changed by this revision. The follow-up recorded in mechanical.assembly.no_change_justified (journal.jsonl line 30): 'A dimension was added to the chassis; no part was added or moved, so the unladen and total masses are unchanged' is contradicted by the numbers: chassis.mass itself moved from 165g to 205g as a direct result of this revision (see [rule]), so the claim that nothing of mass consequence happened, and that only 'a dimension' changed, does not hold.

mechanical.chassis.mass is a mass-property value written by this revision whose stated method (a parts-sheet-row formula) in fact double-counts the wheel-pair mass already present in its base term, as shown under [rule] (frame_and_board=106g + wheel_pair=39.7g + 2 motors at 9.5g = 164.7g, matching the pre-revision chassis.mass of 165g, not the new 205g). A mass derivation that double-counts a component already present in the figure it is built from is not a sound 'stated method' coming from the parts list, even though a source citation is present.

mechanical.gearbox_left.motor_reaction_moment is written as 0.145 N*m via 'derived: [R1.07]*[R1.25]' (design/nodes/mechanical.gearbox_left.json; journal.jsonl rev 29) -- the combined two-motor stall-torque total -- while the structurally identical mechanical.gearbox_right.motor_reaction_moment (journal rev 30) correctly holds the single motor's own reaction, 0.0726 N*m, sourced directly to the Pololu product page. The revision's own no_change_justified reason written onto mechanical.chassis (journal rev 31) states 'the two per-side reactions of 0.0726 N*m sum to the chassis total of 0.145 N*m already carried,' which assumes gearbox_left is 0.0726 N*m -- contradicting the 0.145 N*m actually written there. Summing the two written per-gearbox reactions (0.0726 + 0.145 = 0.2176 N*m) does not balance the chassis's own declared total reaction (0.145 N*m). The revision is therefore internally inconsistent with the design it changes.

mechanical.gearbox_left.motor_reaction_moment = 0.145 N*m is double its structurally identical neighbour mechanical.gearbox_right.motor_reaction_moment = 0.0726 N*m (journal rev 29 vs rev 30), with no stated design asymmetry between the left and right drivetrains (same gear_ratio 2.88, same overall_gear_ratio 148.3, same motor product). It also mismatches the already-present electrical.motor_left.stall_torque = 0.0726 N*m (journal rev 11) for the same physical quantity (the left motor's own stall-torque reaction).

mechanical.chassis.reaction_moment (0.145 N*m, journal rev 4 and rev 31, unchanged) is declared as the total reaction the chassis carries from its two gearbox supports, per the revision's own no_change_justified text. Summing the two newly written per-gearbox reactions (gearbox_left 0.145 N*m + gearbox_right 0.0726 N*m = 0.2176 N*m) does not balance against the chassis's declared total of 0.145 N*m -- an imbalance of about 0.073 N*m, roughly 50% of the declared total.

mechanical.chassis's no_change_justified reason for mechanical.gearbox_left (journal rev 31) reads 'The two per-side reactions of 0.0726 N*m sum to the chassis total of 0.145 N*m already carried' -- but the value the revision actually wrote for gearbox_left is 0.145 N*m, not 0.0726 N*m as the reason assumes. The reason is contradicted by the numbers it is meant to justify, which the rubric names directly as a finding.

mechanical.assembly's mass was changed from 330 g (design/journal.jsonl rev 3/21, formula 'derived: [R11.01] - [R10.03] + [R5.07]*[R5.10]') to 365 g (design/nodes/mechanical.assembly.json, rev 29, formula 'derived: [R11.01] + [R5.07]*[R5.10]'), dropping the bumper-cage subtraction, while the sibling quantity unladen_mass was left unchanged at 165 g ('derived: [R11.01] - [R10.03]'). In the base, mass - unladen_mass = 330 - 165 = 165 g, matching the battery contribution used throughout the design (e.g. electrical.battery_pack.mass = 165 g, journal rev 10); after the revision, mass - unladen_mass = 365 - 165 = 200 g, which no longer matches that battery contribution - a 35 g internal contradiction the revision introduced inside the same node. Separately, the no_change_justified reason the revision wrote on control.balance_loop ('Only overall dimensions were added; the plant mass is unchanged...') is false on the design graph's own numbers: mass changed by 35 g in the same write, yet control.balance_loop.plant_mass (journal rev 30) stayed at the stale pre-revision value of 330 g. The revision is not consistent with the design it changes.

mechanical.assembly's new mass (365 g, design/nodes/mechanical.assembly.json) is inconsistent with its neighbour quantity unladen_mass (165 g, unchanged) once the fixed battery contribution (165 g, used consistently elsewhere, e.g. journal rev 10 electrical.battery_pack.mass) is accounted for: 365-165=200 g, not 165 g. In the base design (journal rev 3) the same comparison (330-165=165) was consistent; the revision's partial edit broke that consistency between two values in the same node.

mechanical.assembly.mass constrains control.balance_loop (constrains edge present in both base and revision) and was changed from 330 g to 365 g (journal rev 3 vs rev 29). The revision's no_change_justified reason on control.balance_loop ('Only overall dimensions were added; the plant mass is unchanged, and the sheet gives no centre-of-mass height for the loop to use.') is contradicted by the numbers: mass did change (by 35 g, ~10.6%), not only the newly-added overall_height/wheel_top_height dimensions, and control.balance_loop.plant_mass remains at the stale value of 330 g (journal rev 30, unchanged from rev 21), inconsistent with the assembly's new 365 g mass.

The no_change_justified reason the revision wrote on control.balance_loop (design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json, journal rev 30) states only dimensions were added and that plant mass is unchanged, but the design graph itself (comparing journal rev 3/21 to rev 29/30) shows mechanical.assembly's mass changed from 330 g to 365 g in the same write. The reason was written in a way that avoids the follow-up update to control.balance_loop.plant_mass that cross §5 / gate check 7 would otherwise require, rather than because no follow-up was genuinely owed - precisely the pattern [rule] names ('a no_change_justified reason written to avoid a follow-up rather than because none is owed'), and it is visible directly in the design graph, not only in a trajectory.

The revision is not consistent with the design it changes: design/nodes/electrical.mcu.json records max_supply_voltage = 60 V sourced to the Atmel ATmega16U4/32U4 datasheet, but parts_sheet.json row R7.09 ('MCU maximum operating voltage (abs. max)'), drawn from that same URL, gives 6.0 V -- a tenfold discrepancy with the revision's own cited source. The revision's own derived supply_voltage_margin (='[R7.09]-[R7.03]'=1.0 V) correctly uses 6.0 V in its arithmetic, underscoring that the separately-written max_supply_voltage field is simply wrong. The revision is also not consistent with this rubric: the margin construction uses an Absolute-Maximum-table rating as 'the limit' against an operating value, which [rule]/[rule] and §1 treat as the 'designing to the absolute maximum rating' antipattern, with no recommended-operating-voltage figure sourced or its absence recorded (parts_sheet.json row R7.05 is null).

supply_voltage_margin is computed as [R7.09]-[R7.03], i.e. the MCU's Absolute-Maximum-Ratings-table supply voltage (6.0 V, from the Atmel datasheet, labelled 'abs. max' in parts_sheet.json) minus the operating supply voltage (5 V, R7.03), using the absolute maximum figure as the limit of a margin comparison against an operating value. Section 1 of the electrical standards states 'design to the recommended operating conditions... absolute maximum ratings are stress ratings only'; parts_sheet.json row R7.05 ('MCU operating voltage', the recommended figure) is null and was neither sourced nor flagged as absent before the abs-max value was substituted as the limit.

electrical.mcu.json's max_supply_voltage is recorded as 60 V, citing the Atmel ATmega16U4/32U4 datasheet. parts_sheet.json row R7.09 ('MCU maximum operating voltage (abs. max)'), drawn from the identical URL, gives 6.0 V. The cited source does not give 60 V -- a tenfold magnitude error. (The companion supply_voltage_margin value, 1.0 V, is itself arithmetically correct because its derivation notation '[R7.09]-[R7.03]' pulls 6.0 V directly from the parts sheet rather than from the erroneous max_supply_voltage field, which only makes the inconsistency within the same node clearer.)

The newly-written max_supply_voltage (60 V, wrong magnitude aside) is drawn from the Absolute Maximum Ratings table (parts_sheet.json R7.09 labels it '(abs. max)') and is used as the fixed 'limit' in the supply_voltage_margin comparison against the operating supply voltage, matching the antipattern's literal trigger: 'Counts when a limit comes from the absolute maximum table.' No recommended-operating-voltage figure (parts_sheet.json R7.05, which is null) was sourced or its absence flagged before the abs-max figure was used as the comparison limit.

design/nodes/electrical.mcu.json records max_supply_voltage = 60 V citing the Atmel ATmega16U4/32U4 datasheet URL, while parts_sheet.json row R7.09 ('MCU maximum operating voltage (abs. max)'), drawn from the identical URL, gives 6.0 V -- the cited source does not contain the value recorded under it, directly matching the observable 'a citation to a datasheet page that does not contain the value.'

electrical.battery_pack.json's new quantity 'motor_runtime' (source 'derived: [R5.03] * [R5.06] / ([R1.01] * [R1.19] * [R4.19])', unit 's', value 3.14) is inconsistent with its own cited arithmetic: using parts_sheet.json rows R5.03=7.2 V, R5.06=2.2 A*h (converted, as the pack's own charge_capacity already does), R1.01=6 V, R1.19=0.42 A, R4.19=2, the formula evaluates to 15.84 W*h / 5.04 W = 3.14 hours, not 3.14 seconds -- a factor-of-3600 unit/conversion mistake making the written value physically wrong. This written-value defect is not excused by the form-2 given-value/unwritten-record/stand-in-absence rules, so the revision is not consistent with the design or with this rubric's unit-arithmetic requirement.

electrical.battery_pack.json's new quantity 'motor_runtime' (unit 's', value 3.14, source 'derived: [R5.03] * [R5.06] / ([R1.01] * [R1.19] * [R4.19])') fails unit consistency: with R5.03=7.2 V, R5.06=2.2 A*h, R1.01=6 V, R1.19=0.42 A, R4.19=2 (parts_sheet.json), the formula is (V*A*h)/(V*A) = h (hours), not seconds; the unit arithmetic does not balance against the stated unit 's' (cross-domain standards §2).

The cited formula's arithmetic evaluates to about 3.14 hours (~11,314 s), but the record states 3.14 s -- a wrong conversion (off by a factor of 3600); it is also physically implausible against the node's own motor_power_draw (18.0 W), under which 15.8 W*h would last about 0.88 h (~3168 s), not 3.14 s.

electrical.driver_left.no_load_current_draw is recorded as 125 A from 'derived: [R1.02] * [R1.06] / [R5.03]'. Using the cited rows (R1.02=6 V, R1.06=150 mA=0.15 A, R5.03=7.2 V), the arithmetic gives 6 x 0.15 / 7.2 = 0.125 A, not 125 A -- a 1000x discrepancy. electrical.driver_right's identical quantity, same formula, correctly reads 0.125 A. battery_pack's no_change_justified claims the no-load figure 'lies inside' the stall-based budget, false for driver_left's own written value (125 A is not inside 1.25 A or 1.8 A). The revision is not consistent with the design it changes or with this rubric's records-and-magnitudes requirements ([rule], [rule]).

electrical.driver_left.json records no_load_current_draw as value 125, unit 'A', source 'derived: [R1.02] * [R1.06] / [R5.03]'. Redoing that arithmetic (R1.02=6 V, R1.06=150 mA=0.15 A, R5.03=7.2 V) gives 6 V x 0.15 A / 7.2 V = 0.125 A, not 125 A: the recorded value is 1000x too large, a unit-prefix/conversion error (the raw mA figure, 150, appears to have been used unconverted and then labelled 'A'). This is a unit-consistency failure in a quantity the revision itself wrote.

Same node/quantity as [rule]: the value (125 A) is not what its own cited derivation gives (0.125 A) -- exactly the 'off by a unit prefix or a wrong conversion' failure this item names. electrical.driver_right's identical quantity (no_load_current_draw = 0.125 A, same formula) is correctly computed, confirming the left node's value is the error.

electrical.driver_left.no_load_current_draw (125 A) does not match the value its own cited derivation computes (0.125 A); the identical formula applied to driver_right correctly yields 0.125 A, showing the cited source does not give the value recorded for driver_left.

battery_pack's no_change_justified entry for electrical.driver_left states 'the no-load figure lies inside it [the stall budget]', but electrical.driver_left.no_load_current_draw is recorded as 125 A -- far above both current_draw (1.25 A) and current_limit (1.8 A) it is claimed to lie inside; the claim contradicts the design graph's own written value.

The revision is not consistent with itself: electrical.battery_cell.json's energy_capacity quantity (design/nodes/electrical.battery_cell.json) is recorded as {source: 'derived: [R5.05] * [R5.06]', unit: 'J', value: 2.64}, but R5.05 (cell nominal voltage, 1.2 V) times R5.06 (capacity, 2200 mA*h = 2.2 A*h) is 2.64 V*A*h = 2.64 W*h = 9504 J, not 2.64 J. The revision's own electrical.battery_pack.json no_change_justified entry calls this same number '2.64 W*h', directly contradicting the unit the revision wrote for it in electrical.battery_cell.json. A revision that mislabels its own newly written quantity, and whose two written records disagree with each other about that quantity's unit, is not consistent with the design it changes or with this rubric's [rule]/[rule] requirements.

electrical.battery_cell.json's energy_capacity quantity is {source: 'derived: [R5.05] * [R5.06]', unit: 'J', value: 2.64}. [R5.05] (1.2 V) times [R5.06] (2200 mA*h = 2.2 A*h) is 2.64 V*A*h, dimensionally W*h, not J; the unit arithmetic the source itself specifies does not balance against the declared unit 'J'. This is a newly written value (absent from the prior revision of electrical.battery_cell.json), so it is judged normally, not under the given-value carve-out.

The magnitude 2.64 matches a watt-hour reading (1.2 V * 2.2 A*h = 2.64 W*h) but is declared under the unit 'J'; 2.64 W*h = 9504 J, so as declared the value is off by a factor of 3600 -- a wrong unit conversion on a newly written quantity, confirmed by the revision's own electrical.battery_pack.json no_change_justified text calling the same figure '2.64 W*h'.

electrical.battery_pack.json's no_change_justified text, written by this revision, states 'Six cells of 2.64 W*h give 15.84 W*h, the pack energy already carried as 15.8 W*h'. The design graph's own record for that same 2.64 figure, electrical.battery_cell.quantities.energy_capacity, declares its unit as 'J', not 'W*h' -- the revision's own claim contradicts the revision's own record of the figure it is built on, which is the stated confirmation condition for [rule] (a claimed result that contradicts the one that exists in the design graph).

The revision is not fully consistent with the design it changes: electrical.imu's current_draw change (rev32, design/nodes/electrical.imu.json) constrains both electrical.control_board and control.balance_loop, but only electrical.control_board received a follow-up (rev33, sensor_power_draw recomputed) or, one hop further, a stated no_change_justified reason (electrical.regulator_5v, rev34); control.balance_loop (design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json, rev30) was rewritten in the same changeset for sample_rate only, with no corresponding update or reason addressing electrical.imu's current-draw change. This is the [rule] violation detailed under that item, and it is what makes the single consistency line unmet.

electrical.imu.current_draw changed (design/nodes/electrical.imu.json, rev32, 0.9 mA → 1.25 mA) and this node's 'constrains' list names both electrical.control_board and control.balance_loop. electrical.control_board was followed up (rev33, sensor_power_draw recomputed from the new current_draw) and, one hop on, electrical.regulator_5v carries a no_change_justified entry (rev34) for that edge. control.balance_loop (design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json, rev30), however, was rewritten in the very same changeset — for sample_rate only — with no update and no no_change_justified entry addressing electrical.imu's current-draw change. The revision's own earlier changes (electrical.imu was only ever created, never previously changed) mean this gap is newly introduced by this revision, not a pre-existing base condition, so it is not exempted by the 'conditions already in the design' rule.

design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json (rev 30, diff-01-of-01.patch lines 16-24) rewrites the 'sample_rate' quantity from {unit: Hz, value: 100} to {unit: ms, value: 8.3}. The directly linked requirement node design/nodes/control.req_loop_rate.json (rev 29) records its own 'sample_rate' as {unit: Hz, value: 120}, and the node that control.balance_loop constrains, design/nodes/firmware.balance_task.json (rev 31), records its 'sample_rate' as {unit: Hz, value: 120}. The base design (journal.jsonl rev 20, 21 and 25, before this revision) held all three consistently in Hz. The revision introduced a unit-kind mismatch for the same field name across directly connected nodes (a rate recorded as a period on one node only), an inconsistency of the revision's own making, not inherited from the base, which makes the revision inconsistent with the design it changes.

design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json's 'sample_rate' quantity (rev 30) is recorded with unit 'ms' and value 8.3, i.e. as a period, while the same field name on the directly connected nodes design/nodes/control.req_loop_rate.json (rev 29) and design/nodes/firmware.balance_task.json (rev 31) is recorded with unit 'Hz' as a rate. A quantity record whose unit does not match the kind of quantity its own name denotes, introduced by the revision itself (the base used Hz, value 100, for this same field), is a defect in the value/unit/source integrity this item requires.

design/nodes/control.balance_loop.json (rev 30, diff hunk 3) changes plant_mass from 330 g ('derived: [R11.01]-[R10.03]+[R5.07]*[R5.10]') to 200 g (bare R11.01 citation), contradicting mechanical.assembly.json (rev 3, unchanged), whose 'mass' quantity still states 330 g via the identical formula and which carries a constrains edge to control.balance_loop. The revision gives no reason for this change (the only no_change_justified entry names control.rate_controller's gain, not the plant_mass edit), and plant_mass now excludes the 165 g battery pack (electrical.battery_pack.mass, 'derived: [R5.07]*[R5.10]') that the robot needs to operate, so the revision is inconsistent with both the sibling node that constrains it and physical sense for what 'plant_mass' must represent.

control.balance_loop's plant_mass changed (330 g -> 200 g, design/journal.jsonl rev 30) and control.balance_loop constrains firmware.balance_task (its own 'constrains' field); firmware.balance_task.json was not touched in this revision and no no_change_justified reason addresses the plant_mass change specifically (the one no_change_justified entry present only names control.rate_controller's gain change). This is a genuine follow-up failure, not a pre-existing condition, since the trigger (a plant_mass change) did not exist in the base design at all.

control.balance_loop.json's no_change_justified text states 'A gain inside the loop does not change ... the plant mass' (design/journal.jsonl rev 30), yet the very same write changes plant_mass from 330 g to 200 g; the stated claim is contradicted by the payload it sits beside, which the diff itself shows.

control.speed_controller.json loop_gain moved from 0.5 (rev24) to 3 (rev29), a 6x rise, while its own source clause claims it was 'lowered to pass less wheel-speed noise to the tilt set-point.' A larger gain passes more such noise, not less; the written value contradicts the written rationale.

Claim: the source text says the loop_gain change was 'lowered to pass less wheel-speed noise to the tilt set-point.' Observation: the journal shows the same quantity moved from 0.5 (rev24) to 3 (rev29), raised not lowered, and a larger gain passes more such noise, not less; the stated result is directly contradicted by the written record.

mechanical.chassis.json (design graph, rev 29) holds reaction_moment = 0.145 N*m, source 'derived: [R1.07] * [R1.25]' (per-motor stall torque times the number of motors, 0.74 kgf*cm * 2), and continuous_reaction_moment = 0.0157 N*m, source only the bare URL https://www.pololu.com/product/3073/specs, which is parts_sheet.json row R1.18 (0.16 kgf*cm, torque at max efficiency) converted by unit alone with no multiplication by [R1.25]. The two values describe the same kind of reaction (drivetrain torque reacted by the chassis) at two duty points but use inconsistent scope -- both motors for the stall figure, one motor for the continuous figure -- with no stated reason for the difference. The revision is therefore not internally consistent with the design it changes.

continuous_reaction_moment (0.0157 N*m, single-motor basis, from parts_sheet.json R1.18) is inconsistent with its sibling quantity on the same node, reaction_moment (0.145 N*m, both-motor basis: 'derived: [R1.07] * [R1.25]'). Both describe the chassis's reaction to drivetrain torque at different duty points, but one is scaled by the number of motors and the other is not, with no stated reason; consistently scaled, the continuous figure should be 0.0314 N*m.

electrical.motor_left's new quantity stall_heat_dissipation is recorded as 90 W with a source formula using R1.01 and R1.03, design/journal.jsonl line 29, design/nodes/electrical.motor_left.json. R1.01 is the motor's rated voltage, 6 V, and R1.03 is its stall current at 6 V, 1.5 A, parts_sheet.json rows R1.01 and R1.03, so the cited arithmetic gives 6 times 1.5 equals 9.0 W, not 90 W, a tenfold discrepancy. The sibling node electrical.motor_right, written in the same revision with the identical constrains list and the identical source formula, design/journal.jsonl line 30, correctly records 9.0 W for the same part. The revision is therefore internally inconsistent with its own stated arithmetic on one of the two nodes it changed, so it is not consistent with the design it changes or with this rubric's reading-by-arithmetic standard.

electrical.motor_left's stall_heat_dissipation is written as 90 W citing a formula using R1.01 and R1.03, design/journal.jsonl line 29, design/nodes/electrical.motor_left.json. R1.01 equals 6 V and R1.03 equals 1.5 A, parts_sheet.json, so the cited arithmetic gives 9.0 W, not 90 W. The sibling node electrical.motor_right, written in the same revision with the identical formula and the identical part data, correctly gives 9.0 W, design/journal.jsonl line 30. The electrical.motor_left value is off by a factor of ten from its own cited source, failing [rule]'s magnitude check.

The revision is not consistent with the design it changes: it recomputes driver current_draw, battery_pack.motor_current_draw and firmware.motor_output.pwm_duty_limit for a higher pack voltage (9 V) using a formula that makes stall-current-derived current fall as voltage rises (design/nodes/electrical.driver_left.json, design/nodes/electrical.battery_pack.json), which is physically backward and understates the true 2.25 A stall-current bound against the driver's 1.8 A peak rating; it also deletes electrical.battery_cell's capacity/mass, electrical.battery_pack's capacity/energy/mass, and control.balance_loop's plant_mass without naming the new cell's chemistry or part, or substituting correct alkaline-cell data, leaving the power budget unable to close ([rule], [rule]) and the battery section unable to show chemistry, discharge rate or voltage-window checks ([rule], [rule], [rule]).

electrical.battery_cell (design/nodes/electrical.battery_cell.json) had its rated_voltage changed from 1.2 V (sourced to the Pololu NiMH AA cell product page) to 1.5 V (sourced only to 'derived: [R5.04]/[R5.10]', a parts-sheet arithmetic expression), and its charge_capacity and mass_per_cell quantities were deleted outright. The new, implicitly-alkaline cell is never given a manufacturer part number or datasheet with revision anywhere in the written nodes, which [rule] requires whenever a part is replaced.

electrical.battery_pack.motor_current_draw (2.0 A) and motor_power_draw (18.0 W) are declared, but the revision deleted the only pack-level capability figures that could close the budget against (charge_capacity 2.2 A*h and energy_capacity 15.8 W*h, present in the base at design/journal.jsonl rev 10, absent from rev 30). With no declared continuous or peak rating of the pack left in the written nodes, the budget cannot be shown to close even once, let alone twice; [rule] is explicitly exempt from the 'conditions already in the design' downgrade, so this is judged, and fails, on the values present.

The revision changes electrical.battery_pack.supply_voltage to 9 V via the parts-sheet row explicitly labelled 'pack nominal voltage (alkaline)' (R5.04), implying a chemistry change, yet no node anywhere states 'alkaline' or names a cell maker/part for it, and electrical.battery_pack.motor_current_draw (2.0 A) is never compared against any sourced maximum discharge rate or published discharge-curve data for that chemistry, as [rule] requires when no sourced rate exists.

electrical.battery_pack.supply_voltage (9 V) and all values derived from it (driver current_draw, pwm_duty_limit) are evaluated only at this single nominal figure; there is no top-of-window (highest open-circuit) or bottom-of-window (sagged, loaded) voltage check anywhere in the written nodes. Because the written supply_voltage value differs from the base's 7.2 V, this sub-check is judged normally rather than as a restated pre-existing condition, and it fails.

design/nodes/electrical.driver_left.json and electrical.driver_right.json: current_draw changed to 1.0 A via 'derived: [R1.02]*[R1.04]/[R5.04]' = 6 V * 1.5 A / 9 V. Using R = V_rated/I_stall = 6 V/1.5 A = 4 ohm, the correct bound at the new pack voltage is I_stall,max = V_max/R = 9 V/4 ohm = 2.25 A per motor, not 1.0 A; the written value is lower even than the motor's 6 V rated stall current (1.5 A), the opposite of [rule]'s required scaling (stall current rises with applied voltage). Because the written current_draw figure differs numerically from the base value (1.25 A), this is judged as a new failure, not a restated pre-existing one.

Comparing the understated current_draw (1.0 A, see [rule]) against current_limit (1.8 A) and output_current (1.5 A) on the same node (design/nodes/electrical.driver_left.json) trivially passes, but the correctly-scaled stall current of 2.25 A exceeds both the 1.8 A peak rating and the DRV8838's minimum 1.9 A overcurrent trip documented in the skill file; the comparison [rule] requires was performed with the wrong current figure and the resulting trip condition is neither shown nor declared to the control or firmware roles.

electrical.battery_pack.supply_voltage (9 V) is declared, but the revision removed charge_capacity (2.2 A*h) and energy_capacity (15.8 W*h), so the pack's rating is left as only a voltage with no current or power capability to balance draws against. 'Redo the balance by reading' cannot be done: there is no supply-side rating left to compare motor_current_draw (2.0 A) or motor_power_draw (18.0 W) with. [rule] is explicitly exempt from the form-2 'given value' and 'unwritten record' downgrades, so this is a fail on the values present.

electrical.battery_pack.supply_voltage (9 V) is the only voltage used throughout (battery_cell.rated_voltage, driver current_draw, firmware.motor_output.pwm_duty_limit all derive from it alone); no top-of-window or sagged-bottom voltage is used anywhere. Since the written supply_voltage value differs from the base's 7.2 V, this is judged as a new, confirmed instance of the antipattern, not a restated pre-existing one.

driver_left/right.current_draw is computed as rated_voltage(6 V) x rated_stall_current(1.5 A) / pack_voltage(9 V) = 1.0 A, which both uses the motor's rated-voltage figures and, by dividing by the higher pack voltage, produces a value lower than even the 6 V-rated stall current itself, rather than scaling the stall current up at the pack's higher voltage as the skill's own procedure (step 1) requires.

The revision is not fully consistent with the design it changes or with this rubric: its new no_change_justified text for electrical.driver_left and electrical.driver_right asserts the DRV8838 driver is adequately sized using the motor's rated-voltage (6 V) stall current of 1.5 A, while the battery pack supplies 7.2 V nominal (up to about 8.4 V fresh), and by the design's own recorded current_limit of 1.8 A the real pack-voltage-scaled stall current (1.8-2.1 A) is at or above that limit -- see [rule] and [rule] findings below.

The change adds quantities to electrical.motor_left/motor_right, firing this item's trigger. The new no_change_justified text on electrical.driver_left/driver_right uses the motor's rated-voltage (6 V) stall current of 1.5 A as the basis for the claim that the driver 'is sized for' it, without scaling to the pack's higher voltage. Redone: R = 6 V/1.5 A = 4 Ohm; at the pack's own nominal voltage (electrical.battery_pack.supply_voltage = 7.2 V, unchanged given value) the stall current is 7.2/4 = 1.8 A, exactly equal to the driver's own recorded current_limit of 1.8 A (electrical.driver_left/right, unchanged given value) -- zero margin, not 'well inside' anything; at the pack's fresh open-circuit top (~8.4 V, per the electrical standards file's own six-NiMH example) it is about 2.1 A, above that 1.8 A limit. This is 'use of the rated-voltage figure at a higher supply,' which the item states fails, and the claim is new text the revision wrote (the base driver nodes, journal rev 13/14, had no no_change_justified field at all), so it is not exempted as a pre-existing condition.

The peak-rating comparison the new no_change_justified text makes (1.5 A stall 'vs' the implied driver sizing) uses the wrong, unscaled current (see [rule]); correctly scaled, the pack-voltage stall current (1.8-2.1 A) is at or above the driver's recorded 1.8 A current_limit, so the 'well inside it' claim fails that comparison. The continuous-rating and minimum-overcurrent-trip comparisons cannot be completed at all because the parts sheet gives no value for them (rows R4.06 'peak output current', R4.07 'peak drive current (absolute max)' and R4.08 'overcurrent protection trip level IOCP' are all null) and no such quantity is recorded on electrical.driver_left/right either; this latter gap is recorded separately as a non-blocking specification defect, not as part of this unmet finding.

The new no_change_justified text for electrical.driver_left and electrical.driver_right compares the driver's sizing against the motor's rated-voltage (6 V) stall current of 1.5 A ('the driver is sized for the 1.5 A stall current') while the pack supplies 7.2 V nominal, up to about 8.4 V fresh -- higher than the motor's 6 V rating. This is exactly the antipattern the skill file names: 'Stall current at the motor's rated voltage... the check uses the pack's highest voltage.' Scaled correctly (R = 4 Ohm), the stall current at the pack's own nominal voltage is already 1.8 A, equal to the driver's recorded 1.8 A current_limit, and about 2.1 A at the pack's fresh top -- above it.

The revision's only substantive written content (design/nodes/control.req_loop_rate.json, journal.jsonl rev 29: sample_rate 100->50 Hz, source '...relaxed to admit slower test builds') is inconsistent with this rubric's own incorporated standards: it is a new written value (differs from the base's 100 Hz, so the 'Conditions already in the design' shield in Section 2's preamble does not apply) that states no ratio to the closed-loop bandwidth and is justified by a non-technical, unsourced convenience reason, matching [rule]'s antipattern and breaching policy rule 6's unexcused-widening rule (no issued specification exists, so no allowance can apply per rule 10). The propagation follow-up at control.balance_loop (journal rev 30, no_change_justified) is correctly executed but does not cure this underlying defect in what the revision itself wrote.

journal.jsonl rev 29 / design/nodes/control.req_loop_rate.json: sample_rate changed from 100 Hz ('design: lowest balance-loop rate the robot is specified to run at') to 50 Hz ('...relaxed to admit slower test builds'). This is a newly written value (differs in number from the base, so the Section 2 preamble's 'Conditions already in the design' exemption does not apply) that states no ratio to the closed-loop bandwidth and is justified by convenience ('admit slower test builds') rather than argued, which is exactly the antipattern the control skill file names: 'Defaulting the sample rate to a round number with no stated ratio ... state the ratio to the closed-loop bandwidth actually achieved, not the number that was easy to pick.'

journal.jsonl rev 29: control.req_loop_rate.sample_rate widened from 100 Hz to 50 Hz, i.e. the stated minimum sampling-rate threshold was relaxed by half, with the justification 'relaxed to admit slower test builds' -- not a sourced bandwidth-ratio analysis. No issued specification exists to supply an allowance (policy rule 10: 'with no issued specification there are no allowances'), and the given reason is not a sourced control-theoretic analysis, so neither of [rule]'s two excuses applies.

electrical.battery_pack.json's payload lists 'constrains': ['mechanical.assembly','firmware.motor_output','electrical.driver_left','electrical.driver_right']. The revision added two brand-new quantities to this node, continuous_motor_current_draw and continuous_motor_power_draw (journal.jsonl rev 33, design/nodes/electrical.battery_pack.json). It wrote a no_change_justified entry for mechanical.assembly (rev 34) and one for firmware.motor_output (rev 35) explaining why those two nodes need no further change, but wrote no follow-up change and no no_change_justified entry naming electrical.driver_left or electrical.driver_right for this new battery_pack quantity (design/nodes/electrical.driver_left.json and electrical.driver_right.json show no no_change_justified field). Since these battery_pack quantities are new (no base value existed before rev 33), this gap is not a pre-existing condition the revision merely re-cited; it is a new inconsistency between the revision's own propagation discipline and the design graph's constrains structure, and with this rubric's [rule]. This makes the single Section 1 line unmet.

electrical.battery_pack's constrains list names mechanical.assembly, firmware.motor_output, electrical.driver_left and electrical.driver_right (design/nodes/electrical.battery_pack.json). The revision added continuous_motor_current_draw and continuous_motor_power_draw to this node (journal rev 33) and recorded no_change_justified reasons on mechanical.assembly (rev 34) and firmware.motor_output (rev 35), but recorded neither a follow-up change nor a no_change_justified entry on electrical.driver_left or electrical.driver_right for this change. Numeric output: continuous_motor_current_draw = 0.7 A, continuous_motor_power_draw = 5.04 W, both unfollowed on two of their four constrained nodes.

mechanical.gearbox_left.json and mechanical.gearbox_right.json's new 'motor_reaction_moment': 0.0726 N*m (source https://www.pololu.com/product/3073/specs) omits the node's own 'gear_ratio': 2.88 field (the external Balboa-kit gear stage), understating the drive's stall-torque reaction the mechanical skill file's own worked example computes as 0.209 N*m per wheel for the identical motor and ratio. mechanical.chassis.json's no_change_justified text ('the two per-side reactions of 0.0726 N*m sum to the chassis total of 0.145 N*m already carried') then relies on this same unscaled figure to justify leaving chassis.reaction_moment unchanged, which the node's own gear_ratio field contradicts.

mechanical.gearbox_left.json and mechanical.gearbox_right.json write 'motor_reaction_moment': 0.0726 N*m in a node that also carries 'gear_ratio': 2.88 and 'overall_gear_ratio': 148.3 (the external Balboa-kit stage). The value used is the motor's own pre-external-stage output (same number and source as electrical.motor_left/right's stall_torque), not multiplied by the node's own 2.88 ratio. The mechanical skill file's worked example, citing the identical motor (product 3073) and the identical external ratio, computes the stall bound at the wheel axle as 0.209 N*m per wheel - about 2.88x the written value - so the written magnitude is inconsistent with its own node's neighbouring gear_ratio quantity and with the sourced worked example for the identical hardware.

mechanical.gearbox_left.json and mechanical.gearbox_right.json's 'constrains' edges name mechanical.chassis, control.balance_loop and firmware.encoder_counter. The no_change_justified entry on mechanical.chassis.json ('The two per-side reactions of 0.0726 N*m sum to the chassis total of 0.145 N*m already carried') is contradicted by the numbers per [rule] (the true per-wheel reaction is about 0.209 N*m, summing to about 0.418 N*m, not 0.145 N*m). The entry on control.balance_loop.json ('a structural load does not change the loop's actuator figures') treats motor_reaction_moment and torque_peak as unrelated, yet control.balance_loop.json's torque_peak and mechanical.chassis.json's reaction_moment use the identical source formula 'derived: [R1.07] * [R1.25]', so the same understatement would carry to torque_peak; this reason is unsupported. The entry on firmware.encoder_counter.json ('the gear ratios are unchanged, so the overall ratio the counter scales by is unchanged') does hold, since encoder scaling depends only on the unchanged gear ratios.

The revision is not consistent with the rubric: electrical.mcu's new supply_voltage_margin quantity (design/nodes/electrical.mcu.json, journal rev 29) is computed from R7.09, the parts sheet's 'MCU maximum operating voltage (abs. max)' row, treating the ATmega32U4's absolute-maximum voltage rating as an operating limit to derive an operating margin. This is the [rule] domain-standard violation and the [rule] skill-file antipattern, both of which are cat. 2 rules with no specific allowance in play (there is no issued specification in form 2 to grant one), so the written value itself is inconsistent with the rubric it is judged against.

electrical.mcu's supply_voltage_margin = [R7.09] - [R7.03] = 6.0 V - 5 V = 1.0 V (design/nodes/electrical.mcu.json, journal rev 29) compares the Absolute Maximum Ratings figure (R7.09, parts_sheet.json, labelled '(abs. max)') with the operating supply_voltage (5 V) to produce an operating-margin quantity. Per [rule] and electrical standards §1 (citing TI SLVSBA4F §6.1 note 1, the same principle this library applies to every part), an absolute maximum rating is a stress rating, not an operating limit, and using it as the limit in a margin comparison fails.

electrical.mcu's supply_voltage_margin (1.0 V, journal rev 29) is computed directly from R7.09, the parts sheet's absolute-maximum voltage rating for the ATmega32U4 (labelled 'MCU maximum operating voltage (abs. max)'), rather than from the datasheet's recommended operating condition. This is precisely the skill file's antipattern: 'Designing to the absolute maximum rating. It is a stress rating, not an operating limit (§1).'
